definition_zh: 合同；契约；收缩；染上（疾病）
definition_en: a written agreement between two sides, or to become smaller, or to catch an illness
core_image: 两双手在纸上按下印章，纸边向里卷起
scene: 签完字，双方各留一份，纸被折好放进公文包。 Both sides signed the contract on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 contract 指「合同」（第 1 个义项：双方签下的书面约定）；句意是双方在周五签了这份合同。

senses.title: A written agreement
senses.definition: a formal written promise made between two or more sides
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方之间作出的正式书面承诺
senses.example: The contract runs for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份合同为期两年。
senses.why: A promise on paper outlives the mood that made it.
senses.whyCN: 写在纸上的承诺，比许下它的心情活得更久。

senses.title: To draw smaller
senses.definition: to become shorter, narrower or tighter
senses.definitionCN: 变得更短、更窄或更紧
senses.example: Metal contracts as it cools.
senses.exampleCN: 金属冷却时会收缩。
senses.why: Cold pulls the pieces closer together.
senses.whyCN: 冷把各个部分拉得更近。

senses.title: To catch an illness
senses.definition: to begin to suffer from a disease
senses.definitionCN: 开始患上某种疾病
senses.example: He contracted a fever in the wet season.
senses.exampleCN: 他在雨季染上了热病。
senses.why: An illness can be picked up the way a habit is.
senses.whyCN: 疾病也能像习惯一样被沾染上身。

intro.en: Contract comes from Latin contrahere, to draw together, built from com-, together, and trahere, to draw or pull.
intro.cn: contract 来自拉丁语 contrahere（拉在一起），由 com-（一起）与 trahere（拉）构成。

items.en: Trahere meant to draw or pull something along.
items.cn: trahere 意为拖或拉某物。

items.en: Contrahere meant to pull parts into a smaller space.
items.cn: contrahere 意为把各部分拉进更小的空间。

items.en: The noun contractus named a drawing together, then a bargain.
items.cn: 名词 contractus 先指拉紧，后指订立的约定。

items.en: French contract named a formal agreement.
items.cn: 法语 contract 指正式的约定。

items.en: English contract kept both the agreement and the shrinking senses.
items.cn: 英语 contract 同时保留约定与收缩两层意思。

items.en: The illness sense grew from the idea of being drawn into.
items.cn: 染病义由被卷入其中的想法发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin drawing base tract-, and the meaning group names other words for agreements and shrinking.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的拉动词基 tract-，近义组列出其他表示约定与收缩的词。

entries.definition: communication or touching between people
entries.definitionCN: 接触；联系

entries.definition: a clear difference between things
entries.definitionCN: 对比；反差

entries.definition: a firm or person hired to do work
entries.definitionCN: 承包商

entries.definition: a formal arrangement accepted by both sides
entries.definitionCN: 协议；约定

entries.definition: to become smaller in size
entries.definitionCN: 缩小；收缩

entries.definition: to get an illness from somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 染上（疾病）

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two sides pulled together by a paper, then move to metal pulled smaller and an illness pulled in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被一纸文书拉到一起的两方开始，再到被拉小的金属，最后到被卷进来的病。

normal.en: Con- is together and tract is pull, so a contract pulls two sides together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，tract 是拉，contract 就是把两方拉到一起。

normal.en: The same pull makes metal shorter and a deal binding.
normal.cn: 同一个拉的动作，让金属变短，也让交易有了约束。

normal.en: A signature turns a talk into a contract.
normal.cn: 一个签名把谈话变成了合同。

normal.en: Cold air contracts a balloon without any paper at all.
normal.cn: 冷空气会让气球收缩，完全不需要纸。

normal.en: A fever can be contracted the way a cold is.
normal.cn: 热病也能像感冒一样被染上。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pulling one sheet tight between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两双手把一张纸在中间拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture a metal band tightening around a barrel.
abstract.cn: 想象一道金属箍在木桶上收紧。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing and drawing the cold inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门关上，把寒气卷进屋里。

examples.en: They signed a contract for the new roof.
examples.cn: 他们为新房顶签了一份合同。

examples.en: The two sides are still under contract.
examples.cn: 双方仍受合同约束。

examples.en: Rubber contracts when it gets cold.
examples.cn: 橡胶遇冷会收缩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contract 记成 con（一起）加 tract（拉）：把两方拉到一起签下的纸，就是合同；把体积往里拉，就是收缩。

root: 源自拉丁语 contrahere（拉在一起），由 con-（一起）与 trahere（拉）构成，后指合同、收缩与染病。

sensesIntro.en: From two sides pulled together by a written promise, to metal pulled smaller, and at last to an illness drawn in.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被书面承诺拉到一起的两方，到被拉小的金属，最后到被卷进来的疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pulling one sheet tight between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双手把一张纸在中间拉紧。

branches.en: A written promise binds two sides into one deal.
branches.cn: 书面承诺把两方绑成一桩交易。

branches.en: The pull shows plainly when metal cools.
branches.cn: 金属冷却时，这个拉的动作看得最清楚。

branches.en: An illness is drawn into the body from outside.
branches.cn: 疾病是从外面被拉进身体里的。

branches.en: Both senses come from one picture of pulling tight.
branches.cn: 两个义项都出自拉紧这一幅画面。

branches.en: What is drawn in can be a size or a sickness.
branches.cn: 被拉进来的，可以是体积，也可以是病。

intro.en: Contract is built on Latin com-, together, plus trahere, to draw.
intro.cn: contract 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 trahere（拉）构成。

latinIntro.en: The drawing base tract- also appears in attract, extract and subtract.
latinIntro.cn: 拉动词基 tract- 也出现在 attract、extract 与 subtract 中。

items.meaning: to draw two sides into one deal
items.meaningCN: 把两方拉进同一桩交易
items.exampleCN: 他们与一位建筑商签了约。

items.meaning: a person or firm that takes work
items.meaningCN: 承接工程的个人或公司

items.example: The contraction of the metal was clear.

items.meaning: to touch or get in touch
to draw one number from another
items.meaningCN: 从一个数里减去另一个数

definition_zh: 从句；分句；（合同、法律的）条款
definition_en: a group of words with its own verb that forms part of a sentence, or a separate condition in a legal document
core_image: 合同上被手指按住的一行小字
scene: 律师把合同推到对面，手指顺着其中一行往下滑。 A single clause in the contract decides who pays.
sceneCN: 这里 clause 指「条款」（第 2 个义项：法律文件中的一项独立规定）；句意是合同里的一条条款决定了由谁付款。

senses.title: A part of a sentence
senses.definition: a group of words that contains a verb and forms part of a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 含有动词、构成句子一部分的一组词
senses.example: The sentence has one main clause and two relative clauses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子有一个主句和两个关系从句。
senses.why: A grammatical clause is a closed unit of meaning, so it took the Latin word for a closing.
senses.whyCN: 语法上的分句是一个闭合的意义单位，因此用了拉丁语表示关闭的词。

senses.title: A condition in a document
senses.definition: a separate item in a contract, treaty or law that states a condition
senses.definitionCN: 合同、条约或法律中规定某项条件的独立条目
senses.example: The contract contains a clause about late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 合同里有一条关于逾期付款的条款。
senses.why: Legal sentences were also divided into closed units, and each item kept the name of a clause.
senses.whyCN: 法律条文同样被分成闭合的单元，每一小条都沿用 clause 之名。

intro.en: Clause comes from a Latin verb meaning to close, and it still means a closed unit of a sentence.
intro.cn: clause 出自拉丁语表示关闭的动词，至今仍指句子中一个闭合的单位。

items.en: Claudere meant to close or shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭或合上。

items.en: Clausa meant a closed section of a text.
items.cn: clausa 指文本中闭合的一段。

items.en: Clause carried the legal sense of a proviso.
items.cn: clause 带有条文式的法律含义。

items.en: English used clause in law before it named grammar.
items.cn: 英语先在法律中使用 clause，后用于语法。

items.en: The grammatical sense is now the everyday one.
items.cn: 语法义如今是日常用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that rhyme or nearly rhyme, while the meaning group names parts of sentences and documents.
note.cn: 形近组列出押韵或近韵的词，近义组列出句子与文件中的成分。

entries.definition: something that makes an event happen
entries.definitionCN: 使某事件发生的原因

entries.definition: a short stop before continuing
entries.definitionCN: 继续之前的短暂停顿

entries.definition: a group of pupils or a lesson
entries.definitionCN: 一群学生或一节课

entries.definition: a small group of words without a full verb
entries.definitionCN: 不含完整动词的一小组词

entries.definition: a condition written into a law or contract
entries.definitionCN: 写入法律或合同的某项条件

entries.definition: one of the parts into which a text is divided
entries.definitionCN: 文本被分成的部分之一

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the closing root, the grammar sense and the contract sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用关闭词根、语法义与合同义。

normal.en: Clause hides the Latin verb to close, so a clause is a closed piece of a sentence.
normal.cn: clause 里藏着拉丁语表示关闭的动词，所以分句是句子里闭合的一块。

normal.en: A clause must have a verb, while a phrase may have none.
normal.cn: 分句必须有动词，短语可以没有。

normal.en: The same word works in grammar and in law, because both divide a text into units.
normal.cn: 同一个词兼用于语法与法律，因为两者都把文本分成单元。

normal.en: An escape clause is a door left open in a contract.
normal.cn: escape clause 是合同里留着一扇开着的门。

normal.en: Clause is one syllable and ends in a soft z sound.
normal.cn: clause 只有一个音节，结尾是柔和的 z 音。

abstract.en: Picture a finger stopping under one short line of small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指停在一行小字下面。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence cut into two blocks by a comma.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子被逗号切成两块。

abstract.en: Picture a contract with one paragraph marked in yellow.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同里有一段被荧光笔标黄。

examples.en: The sentence has one main clause and two relative clauses.
examples.cn: 这个句子有一个主句和两个关系从句。

examples.en: The contract contains a clause about late payment.
examples.cn: 合同里有一条关于逾期付款的条款。

examples.en: They removed the escape clause before signing.
examples.cn: 签约前他们删掉了例外条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「扣」，ause 想成「奥斯」：一扣扣住的一小段，就是分句或条款。

root: 源自拉丁语 claudere（关闭）的分词形式 clausa（闭合的一段），经中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A closed unit of a sentence becomes a closed unit of a law, and both keep one name.
sensesIntro.cn: 句子里闭合的一块，后来变成法律中闭合的一条，两者共用一个名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger holding one printed line in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指按住印刷文本上的一行。

branches.en: Grammar closes a sentence into clauses.
branches.cn: 语法把句子切成闭合的分句。

branches.en: Law closes a document into numbered conditions.
branches.cn: 法律把文件切成编号的条件。

branches.en: Both senses name a closed unit of text.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指文本中闭合的单元。

branches.en: A clause needs its own verb, which a phrase lacks.
branches.cn: 分句需要自己的动词，短语则没有。

branches.en: A clause in a contract states one enforceable condition.
branches.cn: 合同中的一条条款规定一项可执行的条件。

intro.en: The noun takes a plural, an adjective and a prefixed form, and shares a root with close and closure.
intro.cn: 这个名词接复数、形容词与前缀形式，并与 close、closure 同根。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin claudere, to close, which also gave close, closure and enclose.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 claudere（关闭），close、closure、enclose 也源于它。

items.meaning: a sentence part or a legal item
items.example: The clause is easy to miss.

items.meaning: a smaller clause inside a clause
items.exampleCN: 这个次级分句补出一个条件。

items.example: The closure of the road lasted a week.

latinEntries.example: Claudere is the root of clause and close.
latinEntries.exampleCN: claudere 是 clause 与 close 的词根。

definition_zh: 违反；破裂；缺口；（鲸）跃出水面
definition_en: a break in a law, wall, or relationship; also a whale's leap from water
core_image: 城墙被撞开一个大缺口，士兵从裂口中涌入；也有鲸鱼破水腾空的画面
scene: 律师把文件推到桌上。 The company's failure to deliver was a clear breach of contract.
sceneCN: 这里 breach 是「违反」（第 1 个义项：违背契约、法律）；句意是公司未能交货，明显违反了合同。

derivatives.zh: 由复合构成，义为「（旧法）毁弃婚约」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「未被攻破的」

senses.title: A breaking of a law or agreement
senses.definition: an act of failing to obey a law or carry out an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 不遵守法律或不履行协议的行为
senses.example: Late payment counts as a breach of the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 迟付租金即构成违反租约。
senses.why: The word means break, and a broken promise is the legal form of a broken thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义就是「破」，而被打破的诺言正是「破物」在法律上的形态。

senses.title: A gap made in a wall or defense
senses.definition: a hole or opening forced in a wall, barrier, or defense
senses.definitionCN: 在墙、屏障或防御中强行打开的洞口
senses.example: The siege guns opened a breach in the rampart.
senses.exampleCN: 攻城炮在壁垒上轰开一个缺口。
senses.why: The physical breaking of stone is the word's oldest workplace.
senses.whyCN: 石头的物理破裂是这个词最古老的用武之地。

senses.title: A rupture in a relationship
senses.definition: a serious break in friendship, relations, or unity
senses.definitionCN: 友谊、邦交或团结上的严重破裂
senses.example: The remark caused a breach between the two families.
senses.exampleCN: 那句话造成两家关系破裂。
senses.why: What holds between people is pictured as a wall, so a quarrel breaches it.
senses.whyCN: 人与人之间的维系被想象为一堵墙，争吵便在其上破出裂口。

senses.title: A violation of a duty or confidence
senses.definition: a failure to fulfill a duty or keep confidence
senses.definitionCN: 未能尽责或保守信赖
senses.example: Leaking the file was a breach of trust.
senses.exampleCN: 泄露档案是背信行为。
senses.why: Trust is an invisible wall; letting it crack is the moral twin of opening a rampart.
senses.whyCN: 信赖是无形的墙，让它裂开与轰开壁垒在道德上互为镜像。

senses.title: A whale's leap from the water
senses.definition: an instance of a whale rising clear out of the water and falling back
senses.definitionCN: 鲸整身跃出水面再落回的动作
senses.example: A humpback breached right beside the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 一头座头鲸就在小船旁跃出水面。
senses.why: The whale is pictured as breaking through the sea's surface, a wall of water.
senses.whyCN: 鲸被想象为冲破海面这堵「水墙」，故借得此名。

senses.title: A gap in a line of duty to be filled
senses.definition: a gap in defense or service that someone must fill, as in stepping into the breach
senses.definitionCN: 防御或事务中的空缺，需要有人填补，如 step into the breach
senses.example: When the manager resigned, she stepped into the breach.
senses.exampleCN: 经理辞职后，她挺身补位。
senses.why: A broken wall demands defenders; a broken roster does too.
senses.whyCN: 破墙需要人守，人事的破口同样需要人补。

senses.title: An infringement of privacy or security
senses.definition: unauthorized access to data, premises, or personal space
senses.definitionCN: 对数据、场所或私人空间的未授权进入
senses.example: The database breach exposed millions of records.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库失守暴露了数百万条记录。
senses.why: Modern walls are made of code, and breaking them keeps the old name.
senses.whyCN: 现代的墙由代码筑成，攻破它们仍沿用旧名。

senses.title: A breach of the peace
senses.definition: conduct that disturbs public order, a legal term
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱公共秩序的行为，法律术语
senses.example: The argument on the steps amounted to a breach of the peace.
senses.exampleCN: 台阶上的争吵已构成扰乱治安。
senses.why: Public order is the city's wall; disorder breaches it by definition.
senses.whyCN: 公共秩序是城市之墙，失序按定义即在其上破口。

intro.en: Breach is the Anglo-Norman form of break, taken from Old French breche, itself Germanic in origin.
intro.cn: breach 是 break 的盎格鲁-诺曼形式，取自古法语 breche，而 breche 本身源自日耳曼语。

items.en: A reconstructed root *brekan meant to break, common across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *brekan 意为打碎，通行于各日耳曼语言。

items.en: Old English brecan meant to break, giving modern break.
items.cn: 古英语 brecan 意为打破，演变为现代 break。

items.en: Frankish speech gave Old French breche, a breaking or gap.
items.cn: 法兰克语使古法语产生 breche，意为破裂、缺口。

items.en: Middle English took breach from Anglo-Norman and Old French, at first of broken walls.
items.cn: 中古英语经盎格鲁-诺曼语与古法语借入 breach，最初指被攻破的城墙。

items.en: Legal use flourished: breach of contract, breach of the peace, breach of promise.
items.cn: 法律用法大兴：违约、扰乱治安、毁约诸语成型。

items.en: Modern English adds data breaches and the whale's acrobatic breach.
items.cn: 现代英语又添数据泄露与鲸鱼跃身之义。

note.en: Breach is break's Norman twin; beware the spelling pair breach and breech.
note.cn: breach 是 break 的诺曼孪生词；注意 breach 与 breech 这对拼写近亲。

entries.definition: to separate into pieces
entries.definitionCN: 打破；同源本土形式

entries.definition: the rear of a gun or a breech birth
entries.definitionCN: 炮闩；臀位分娩；同音异源

entries.definition: the sandy shore
entries.definitionCN: 海滩；仅差一个字母

entries.definition: dialect, given to breaking fences
entries.definitionCN: 方言：爱越栏的（牲畜）

entries.definition: to raise a subject; to pierce a cask
entries.definitionCN: 提出（话题）；凿穿；拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an act of breaking a rule or right
entries.definitionCN: 违犯；侧重规则与权利

entries.definition: a sudden breaking apart
entries.definitionCN: 破裂；侧重物理或组织断裂

entries.definition: a crack or split in a relationship
entries.definitionCN: 裂隙；与 breach 的关系义相近但程度较缓

entries.definition: an encroachment on rights
entries.definitionCN: 侵权；多用于知识产权与权利

entries.definition: a stepping over a moral limit
entries.definitionCN: 越界；道德或宗教色彩更浓

normalIntro.en: Breach is simply break in Norman dress; a breach is where something has broken.
normalIntro.cn: breach 就是穿着诺曼外衣的 break：breach 即「破」之所在。

normal.en: breach and break share one Germanic root.
normal.cn: breach 与 break 同出一个日耳曼词根。

normal.en: the route was Old French breche, a gap.
normal.cn: 途经古法语 breche，意为缺口。

normal.en: breach of contract is the legal star use.
normal.cn: breach of contract 是法律上的明星用法。

normal.en: breech with two e's belongs to guns and births.
normal.cn: 双 e 的 breech 属于炮闩与臀位。

normal.en: whales breach by breaking the surface.
normal.cn: 鲸的 breach 是破水而出。

abstract.en: Stone broken by cannon; trust broken by a leak: same shape, different matter.
abstract.cn: 炮弹碎石头，泄密碎信任：形同而质异。

abstract.en: Every breach is an invitation written in a broken edge.
abstract.cn: 每一道缺口都是写在破碎边缘的请柬。

abstract.en: What is breached must be manned or mended.
abstract.cn: 破口必须有人把守，或者被修补。

examples.en: Publishing the memo would breach her confidentiality agreement.
examples.cn: 发表那份备忘录将违反她的保密协议。

examples.en: Water poured through the breach in the flood wall.
examples.cn: 洪水从防洪墙的缺口涌入。

examples.en: Neither side wanted a permanent breach in the alliance.
examples.cn: 双方都不希望同盟出现永久性裂痕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不理契」——对契约「不理不睬」就是违约：breach of contract。

sensesIntro.en: From broken walls to broken laws, broken trust, broken relations, and even the whale breaking the sea's skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项由破墙到破法、破信、破情，乃至鲸鱼破开海面之皮。

core.cn: 核心意象：一堵墙上新开的洞——有什么东西破了进来或出去

branches.en: the physical break: ramparts, sea surface, firewalls of code
branches.cn: 物理之破：壁垒、海面、代码防火墙

branches.en: the legal break: contracts, trust, public peace
branches.cn: 法律之破：契约、信赖、公共安宁

branches.en: the human break: friendships torn open
branches.cn: 人心之破：友谊被撕开

definition_zh: 负债；责任；不利条件
definition_en: a legal or financial obligation to pay or do something; something that causes risk or difficulty
core_image: 一个人的脚上拴着一块大铁球，铁球上刻着「欠债必须还」，旁边摆着一份写着 liability 的表格
scene: 公司财务报表的右侧列着各种要付的钱：应付账款、长期借款、应计费用。 Every liability on the balance sheet must be matched against an asset.
sceneCN: 这里 liability 指「公司负债」（第 2 个义项：公司财务上应支付的债务）；句意为资产负债表上总负债首次超过了总资产。图中可辨识物件：资产负债表、铁球、欠债数字。

pos.zh: 负债（可数/不可数）；责任（可数）

derivatives.zh: 联络（同拉丁词根但义不同）

senses.title: legal responsibility
senses.definition: a legal obligation to do or pay something
senses.definitionCN: 法律上做某事或付钱的义务
senses.example: The company denied all liability for the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 公司否认对事故负有任何法律责任。
senses.why: liable 'legally bound' + -ity makes the noun of the obligation.
senses.whyCN: liable「法律上有约束力的」+ -ity 就是这种义务的名词。

senses.title: financial debt or obligation
senses.definition: an amount owed in a company's or person's balance sheet
senses.definitionCN: 公司或个人资产负债表上所欠的金额
senses.example: Mortgages are long-term liabilities for households.
senses.exampleCN: 房贷是家庭的长期负债。
senses.why: A financial debt is a liability, something that binds you to pay.
senses.whyCN: 一笔财务债务就是 liability，绑着你去付钱。

senses.title: something that makes you liable
senses.definition: a person or thing that causes risk or exposure
senses.definitionCN: 带来风险或暴露的人或事
senses.example: His reckless driving made him a liability to the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他鲁莽的驾驶让他成了车队的负担。
senses.why: Something that can make you bound to pay is itself a liability.
senses.whyCN: 任何能让你变得要出钱的东西本身就是 liability。

senses.title: tax or other duty
senses.definition: an amount due to a government or authority
senses.definitionCN: 欠政府或当局的金额
senses.example: Tax liabilities rise as profits grow.
senses.exampleCN: 利润增加，应纳税额也跟着上涨。
senses.why: Any amount you are bound to pay is a liability.
senses.whyCN: 任何你必须付的金额都是 liability。

senses.title: limited liability
senses.definition: a legal structure where owners are only responsible for their investment
senses.definitionCN: 所有者仅对其投资负责的法律结构
senses.example: A limited liability company protects personal savings.
senses.exampleCN: 有限责任公司保护了个人的储蓄。
senses.why: The concept of liability is narrowed to protect owners.
senses.whyCN: liability 的概念被收窄来保护所有者。

senses.title: professional liability
senses.definition: legal responsibility of a professional for errors in work
senses.definitionCN: 专业人士对其工作失误的法律责任
senses.example: Doctors buy liability insurance for malpractice claims.
senses.exampleCN: 医生买职业责任险来应对医疗事故索赔。
senses.why: Professionals are bound to their clients for mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士对其客户的失误有约束力。

senses.title: contractual obligation
senses.definition: an obligation written into a contract between parties
senses.definitionCN: 合同中写明的各方之间的义务
senses.example: The liability to deliver expired when the contract terminated.
senses.exampleCN: 合同终止时，交货义务也过期了。
senses.why: Contracts create binding duties, which are liabilities.
senses.whyCN: 合同创造了有约束力的责任，就是 liabilities。

senses.title: environmental liability
senses.definition: legal obligation to clean up pollution or pay for harm
senses.definitionCN: 清理污染或赔偿损害的法律义务
senses.example: The old factory faces environmental liabilities from decades of waste.
senses.exampleCN: 老工厂因几十年的废弃物面临环境责任。
senses.why: A newer application of the general 'bound to pay' sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是「必须付钱」这个一般义的一个新应用。

intro.en: Liability comes from liable, which comes from Old French lier 'to bind'. Liability is the quality of being bound.
intro.cn: liability 来自 liable，后者来自古法语 lier「绑缚」。liability 就是「被绑着」的状态。

items.en: Latin ligare meant 'to bind'; it gave rise to liare, the Vulgar Latin for 'to bind, tie'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为「绑缚」，它产生了通俗拉丁语 liare「绑、系」。

items.en: Old French lier 'to bind, tie' came from Vulgar Latin liare.
items.cn: 古法语 lier「绑、系」来自通俗拉丁语 liare。

items.en: Middle English liabill meant 'legally bound, answerable'; it came from Old French lier.
items.cn: 中古英语 liabill 意为「法律上有约束力的、应负责的」，来自古法语 lier。

items.en: The suffix -ity (Latin -itas via French) turns the adjective liable into the noun liability.
items.cn: 后缀 -ity（拉丁语 -itas 经法语）把形容词 liable 变成名词 liability。

items.en: The balance-sheet sense 'debts owed' developed by the 17th century, as a debt binds you.
items.cn: 资产负债表上的「所欠债务」义在 17 世纪形成，因为债务就是绑着你的东西。

items.en: Etymology solid; ligare is well attested in classical Latin.
items.cn: 词源可靠；ligare 在古典拉丁语中有充分文献。

note.en: Look-alikes share the lig- bind root; near meanings are obligations or debts.
note.cn: 形近共享 lig-「绑」词根；近义是义务或债务。

entries.definition: Legally bound or responsible; liability is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上有约束力的或应负责的；liability 是它的名词。

entries.definition: A band of tissue that binds bones together.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨头绑在一起的一条组织。

entries.definition: To bind morally or legally; same lig- root.
entries.definitionCN: 在道德或法律上约束；同 lig- 词根。

entries.definition: To communicate and coordinate; from the same lier 'to bind'.
entries.definitionCN: 沟通协调；来自同一个 lier「绑」。

entries.definition: A specific sum owed; liability is broader and includes non-monetary obligations too.
entries.definitionCN: 所欠的一笔具体金额；liability 更宽，也包括非金钱义务。

entries.definition: A duty one is bound to perform; liability is specifically legal/financial.
entries.definitionCN: 被约束必须履行的义务；liability 特指法律/财务上的。

entries.definition: A general duty to act, not necessarily legal or financial.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性的行动义务，不一定是法律或财务的。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实配对。

normal.en: Latin ligare 'to bind' → Old French lier → liable → liability.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ligare「绑缚」→ 古法语 lier → liable → liability。

normal.en: liable = bound; liability = the state of being bound.
normal.cn: liable = 被绑住的；liability = 被绑住的状态。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: total liabilities, financial liability, limited liability, liability insurance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：total liabilities 总负债、financial liability 财务负债、limited liability 有限责任、liability insurance 责任险。

normal.en: lig- root: ligament (body), oblige (duty), liaise (connect).
normal.cn: lig- 词根：ligament（身体里的韧带）、oblige（义务）、liaise（联络）。

normal.en: Balance sheet: assets = what you own, liabilities = what you owe.
normal.cn: 资产负债表：assets = 你拥有的，liabilities = 你欠下的。

abstract.en: Picture a man chained to a pile of coins that grows bigger every month.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人被铁链拴在一堆每个月都在长大的硬币上。

abstract.en: Picture Latin ligare: ropes tying you to what you owe.
abstract.cn: 想象拉丁语 ligare：绳子把你绑在你欠的东西上。

abstract.en: Picture a company's balance sheet as a seesaw: assets on one side, liabilities on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象公司的资产负债表是一架跷跷板：一边是资产，一边是负债。

examples.en: The startup took on significant liabilities to fund its rapid expansion.
examples.cn: 那家初创公司为快速扩张承担了大量负债。

examples.en: Owners of a limited liability company are not personally on the hook for its debts.
examples.cn: 有限责任公司的所有者不亲自替公司的债务背锅。

examples.en: The manufacturer faces product-liability claims from thousands of injured consumers.
examples.cn: 该制造商面临数千名受伤消费者的产品责任索赔。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CORE: being bound by law.
branches.cn: 法律核心：被法律绑着。

definition_zh: 原告；起诉方；提出请求的一方
definition_en: the party who brings a civil case against another
core_image: 一叠写满委屈的纸被推过桌面，第一页最上面写着「我要求」，对面的人只看不接
scene: 开庭前，提起诉讼的一方坐在走廊长椅上，把请求赔偿的清单又数了一遍。 The plaintiff listed every loss in the claim before the hearing began.
sceneCN: 这里 plaintiff 指在民事案件中提起诉讼、要求救济的一方（第 1 个义项：提起民事诉讼的一方）；句意：开庭前，这名原告在请求书中逐项列出了所有损失。图中可辨识物件：走廊长椅、赔偿清单、文件夹、法庭门。

pos.zh: 原告；起诉方（民事案件中提出请求的一方）

collocations.phrase: a plaintiff in a civil action

derivatives.zh: 诉苦；申诉（书面或旧式用法）

senses.title: The party who brings a civil case
senses.definition: the person or body that starts a civil action against another
senses.definitionCN: 对他人提起民事诉讼的个人或机构
senses.example: The plaintiff listed every loss in the claim before the hearing began.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前，原告在请求书中逐项列出了所有损失。
senses.why: The word is built from the verb of complaining, so the party is named by the act of bringing a grievance before a court.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「诉苦」的动词构成，所以这一方是按「把委屈带到法院」这个动作来命名的。

senses.title: The complaining party, literally
senses.definition: literally, the one who complains; the older force of the word
senses.definitionCN: 字面上指诉苦的人，这是这个词较早的力道
senses.example: In the old record the plaintiff is simply called the complainant.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧档案里，原告干脆就被称作「申诉人」。
senses.why: The French participle meant 'complaining', and the legal role grew out of that plain human act of stating a grievance.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语分词本意就是「诉苦的」，法律角色正是从「说出委屈」这一平常举动中长出来的。

senses.title: The party who files first
senses.definition: the party whose filing starts the clock of the case
senses.definitionCN: 其立案动作使案件时间开始走表的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff filed on Monday, and the summons went out on Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 原告周一立案，传票周二就发出去了。
senses.why: Procedure assigns the first move to one side, and that move is what makes the other side a defendant.
senses.whyCN: 程序把第一步分给一方，而正是这一步使另一方成为被告。

senses.title: The party seeking a remedy
senses.definition: the party asking the court for money, an order or another remedy
senses.definitionCN: 向法院请求金钱、命令或其他救济的一方
senses.example: As plaintiff, the tenant asked for the return of the deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 作为原告，租客要求返还押金。
senses.why: A case exists because someone wants something from the court, and the word marks that side of the demand.
senses.whyCN: 案件之所以存在，是因为有人想从法院得到什么，这个词就标记提出要求的那一侧。

senses.title: The first name in a case title
senses.titleCN: 案件名称中排在前面的当事方
senses.definition: in the style 'A v. B', the party named before the versus
senses.definitionCN: 在「甲诉乙」式名称中，排在「诉」之前的那一方
senses.example: The reporter read the case name with the plaintiff first.
senses.exampleCN: 记者念出案件名称时，原告排在首位。
senses.why: Court style fixes the order, and the first slot belongs to the one who brought the complaint, a rule still visible in case citations.
senses.whyCN: 法庭体例固定了顺序，第一格属于提出申诉的人，这一规则至今仍能在案件引证中看到。

senses.title: The party with the initial burden
senses.definition: the party who must first prove the basic elements of the claim
senses.definitionCN: 必须先证明请求基本要件的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff had to prove that the signature was genuine.
senses.exampleCN: 原告必须证明那个签名是真的。
senses.why: Whoever asserts must prove, so the procedural word also marks the side that carries the first load of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 谁主张谁举证，所以这个程序用语也标记首先承担证据重量的一侧。

senses.title: The party who starts arbitration
senses.definition: the party who brings a claim before an arbitrator or tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 向仲裁员或裁判庭提出请求的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff in the arbitration was a supplier from abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁中的原告是一家境外供应商。
senses.why: The same claim-and-answer structure appears outside court, and the label follows the claimant into private forums.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「请求—答辩」结构出现在法院之外，这个标签便随请求人进入私人裁判场合。

senses.title: An accuser in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, anyone who publicly accuses another of wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指公开指控他人有错的人
senses.example: The pamphlet cast the widow as plaintiff against the guild.
senses.exampleCN: 那本小册子把这位寡妇写成了控告行会的原告。
senses.why: Before the word narrowed to civil procedure, it named any accuser, and historical writing still uses that wider reach.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词收窄为民事程序之前，它指任何指控者，历史文字仍保留这一较宽的范围。

intro.en: Plaintiff comes from Old French plaintif 'complaining', from plainte 'complaint', from Latin planctus 'lamentation', the noun of plangere 'to beat the breast'. The legal sense grew from the plain act of stating a grievance.
intro.cn: plaintiff 来自古法语 plaintif「诉苦的」，经 plainte「申诉」上溯拉丁 planctus「哀号」，即 plangere「捶胸」的名词。法律义从「说出委屈」这一平常动作中生长出来。

items.en: Plangere meant to beat or strike, especially the breast in grief, and so to lament. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: plangere 意为击打，尤指悲伤时捶胸，因而意为哀号。其更深来源属来源不确定。

items.en: Planctus was the noun of that beating and wailing: a lamentation, a loud complaint. It supplies the stem seen in plaintive and plaint.
items.cn: planctus 是「捶打与号哭」的名词：哀号、高声诉苦。它提供了 plaintive 与 plaint 中可见的词干。

items.en: Plainte meant a complaint or lament in French, covering both the sound of grief and the formal statement of a grievance.
items.cn: 法语 plainte 指申诉或哀诉，既指悲伤的声音，也指正式提出的不满。

items.en: The adjective plaintif meant 'complaining', and it could stand as a noun for the person who complains, the exact shape English borrowed.
items.cn: 形容词 plaintif 意为「诉苦的」，可作名词指诉苦的人，英语借入的正是这个形态。

items.en: From the fourteenth century English used plaintiff for the party who brings a complaint to court, pairing it with defendant.
items.cn: 十四世纪起，英语用 plaintiff 指把申诉带到法院的一方，并与 defendant 配对使用。

items.en: The word narrowed to civil procedure, where it means the party who sues, while the older sense of any accuser survives only in historical prose.
items.cn: 这个词收窄为民事程序用语，指提起诉讼的一方；而「任何指控者」的旧义只留在历史叙述中。

note.en: Group one separates the complaint, the sad adjective, the unrelated look-alike and the related word with another prefix; group two sets the role against the other names for a claimant.
note.cn: 第一组区分申诉本身、表示哀伤的形容词、无关的形近词，以及带另一个前缀的同根词；第二组把这个角色与请求人的其他称呼作对照。

entries.definition: A complaint or lament, especially in literary or older legal prose; plaintiff is the person, not the text.
entries.definitionCN: 指申诉或哀诉，多见于文学或较早的法律文字；plaintiff 是人，不是文本。

entries.definition: Sounding sad or mournful; it describes a tone, never a party in a case.
entries.definitionCN: 听起来哀伤的；它描述语气，从不指案件中的一方。

entries.definition: Simple or flat, from Latin planus 'flat'. It resembles plaint but has no connection with complaining.
entries.definitionCN: 简单的、平坦的，来自拉丁 planus「平」。它形似 plaint，却与诉苦毫无关系。

entries.definition: A grievance or its formal statement, from the same wailing verb with a prefix meaning 'together'; it is not the party.
entries.definitionCN: 指不满或其正式陈述，同出「哀号」动词，前缀意为「共同」；它不是当事方。

entries.definition: The possessive form marking something belonging to the party, not a second role.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，表示属于该当事方之物，不是第二个角色。

entries.definition: The party making a claim, common in tribunals and benefit cases; plaintiff is the standard court term in civil suits.
entries.definitionCN: 提出请求的一方，常用于裁判庭与福利案件；plaintiff 是民事法庭的标准用语。

entries.definition: The party who files a petition, as in divorce or family cases, where the word often replaces plaintiff.
entries.definitionCN: 提交呈请书的一方，如在离婚或家事案件中，常用它代替 plaintiff。

entries.definition: The person who makes a complaint, sometimes the victim or the reporting party rather than the suing party.
entries.definitionCN: 提出投诉的人，有时指受害人或者报案人，而不一定是起诉方。

entries.definition: Any party to a lawsuit; plaintiff names only the side that brings the claim.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中的任何一方；plaintiff 只指提出请求的那一侧。

entries.definition: The party who must answer the claim, the mirror image of the plaintiff.
entries.definitionCN: 必须对请求作答的一方，正是原告的镜像。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real verb of wailing, the real look-alike plain and the real court pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「哀号」动词、真实的形近词 plain，以及真实的法庭配对。

normal.en: Plangere is to beat the breast: the plaintiff is the one who brings the lament to court.
normal.cn: plangere 是捶胸：原告就是把哀诉带进法院的那个人。

normal.en: Plain means flat, not complaining: one letter alike, two unrelated origins.
normal.cn: plain 意为平坦，不是诉苦；字母相近，来源却全不相干。

normal.en: Plaint is the complaint, plaintiff is the person, plaintive is the tone.
normal.cn: plaint 是申诉，plaintiff 是人，plaintive 是语气。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: plaintiff and defendant, claim and answer.
normal.cn: 这组配对是固定的：原告与被告，请求与答辩。

normal.en: Whoever files first becomes the plaintiff and puts the other side in the answering seat.
normal.cn: 先立案的人成为原告，并把另一方放进应诉的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of grievance sheets pushed across a desk, first line reading I demand.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠申诉纸被推过桌面，第一行写着「我要求」。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the first name on the docket is the one who spoke first.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，日程表上的第一个名字，正是最先开口的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture grief turned into a document: the wail becomes a claim with numbered paragraphs.
abstract.cn: 想象悲伤被做成一份文件：号哭变成分条列项的请求。

examples.en: The plaintiff asked for the deposit back and won.
examples.cn: 原告要求返还押金，并且胜诉。

examples.en: A plaintiff must prove the elements of the claim one by one.
examples.cn: 原告必须逐项证明请求的各个要件。

examples.en: The plaintiff and the defendant agreed to mediate before trial.
examples.cn: 原告与被告在开庭前同意调解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑泪啼夫」——哭着捶胸、把委屈递上法庭的那个人 → 原告

root: 古法语 plaintif（诉苦的），源自 plainte（申诉），上溯拉丁 planctus（哀号），即 plangere（捶胸、哀哭）的名词。plangere 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the civil claimant, through the literal complainer, the first filer, the seeker of a remedy, the first name in a title, the initial burden, the arbitration claimant, and the older accuser.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从民事原告开始，经字面的诉苦者、先立案者、寻求救济者、案件名称的首位、先负举证责任者、仲裁请求人，最后到较早的控诉者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of grievance sheets pushed across a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠申诉纸被推过桌面。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the legal party grows straight out of the plain act of complaining.
branches.cn: 来源：法律上的当事方直接由「诉苦」这一平常动作长成。

branches.en: THE FIRST MOVE: filing is what turns a grievance into a case.
branches.cn: 第一步：立案这个动作把委屈变成案件。

branches.en: THE DEMAND: the party is defined by what it asks the court to give.
branches.cn: 要求：这一方由它向法院请求什么来定义。

branches.en: THE PAPER AND THE PROOF: the first name in the title and the first load of evidence belong to the same side.
branches.cn: 文书与举证：名称的首位与第一批证据都属于同一侧。

branches.en: THE WIDER FORUMS: arbitration keeps the role, and older prose extends it to any accuser.
branches.cn: 更宽的场域：仲裁保留了这一角色，较早的文字则把它扩展到任何指控者。

intro.en: Plaintiff is a French adjective frozen into a legal noun, built on a Latin noun of wailing.
intro.cn: plaintiff 是一个冻结为法律名词的法语形容词，建立在拉丁「哀号」名词之上。

latinIntro.en: The base is plangere 'to beat the breast' and its noun planctus 'lamentation'; French added the adjective ending and English kept the whole shape.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是 plangere「捶胸」及其名词 planctus「哀号」；法语加上形容词词尾，英语把整个形态保留下来。

items.meaning: to beat, strike the breast, lament

items.meaningCN: 捶打；哀号（名词词尾把动作转成声音与事件）

items.example: The suffix made the participle an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 诉苦的（形容词化，随后可作名词）
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述诉苦的人。

items.structure: plaintif used as an English legal noun
items.meaning: the party who brings the complaint
items.meaningCN: 提出申诉的一方（形容词名词化，指案件中的角色）
申诉；哀诉（英语中缩短的形式）
哀伤的（形容词后缀把申诉转成语调）
items.example: A plaintive note ended the letter.
items.exampleCN: 信的结尾是一句哀伤的调子。

definition_zh: 被告；被起诉或被指控的一方；（旧）辩护者
definition_en: the party against whom a claim or a charge is brought
core_image: 被告席前一个人站着，桌上摊着起诉书，背后是旁听席，法官的目光正落在他身上
scene: 开庭那天，被指控的一方站在席位前，手里攥着起诉书副本，逐条否认。 The defendant denied every charge read aloud in court.
sceneCN: 这里 defendant 指案件中被指控、被起诉的一方（第 1 个义项：刑事被告）；句意：这名被告对庭上宣读的每一项指控都予以否认。图中可辨识物件：被告席、起诉书副本、法官席、旁听席。

pos.zh: 被告（刑事案件中被指控者，或民事案件中被起诉者）

collocations.phrase: the defendant in a criminal case

senses.title: The accused in a criminal case
senses.definition: the person charged with an offence and required to answer it in court
senses.definitionCN: 被控犯罪、必须在法庭上作出答辩的人
senses.example: The defendant denied every charge read aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 被告对庭上宣读的每一项指控都予以否认。
senses.why: The word is the present participle of the verb 'to defend', so the accused is literally the one doing the defending in the legal contest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是动词「辩护」的现在分词，所以被告字面上就是在这场法律较量中「进行防守」的那一方。

senses.title: The party sued in a civil case
senses.definition: the party against whom a civil claim is brought
senses.definitionCN: 被提起民事请求的一方
senses.example: The defendant company argued that the contract had never been signed.
senses.exampleCN: 被告公司辩称那份合同从未签署。
senses.why: Civil and criminal procedure share the same structure of claim and answer, so one word serves both sides of the court system.
senses.whyCN: 民事与刑事程序共享「请求—答辩」的同一结构，所以一个词就覆盖了法院体系的两侧。

senses.title: The answering party, neutrally
senses.definition: the party that must respond to any formal claim, without implying guilt
senses.definitionCN: 必须对任何正式请求作出回应的一方，不含罪责暗示
senses.example: Each defendant was given a copy of the petition.
senses.exampleCN: 每一位应诉方都拿到了一份请求书副本。
senses.why: Procedure needs a neutral label for the side that answers, and the word supplies it without the moral weight of 'guilty'.
senses.whyCN: 程序需要一个中性的标签来指作答的一方，这个词正好提供，而不带「有罪」的道德重量。

senses.title: The party carrying the burden of answer
senses.definition: the party who must meet the claim with evidence and argument
senses.definitionCN: 必须以证据和论证来应对请求的一方
senses.example: As defendant, the hospital had to show that its staff had followed procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 作为被告，医院必须证明其员工遵守了程序。
senses.why: Once a claim is filed, the burden of answering shifts to this party, so the word also marks who must produce the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 请求一旦提出，作答的责任就转到这一方，所以这个词也标记谁必须拿出证据。

senses.title: The second name in a case title
senses.titleCN: 案件名称中排在后面的当事方
senses.definition: in the style 'A v. B', the party named after the versus
senses.definitionCN: 在「甲诉乙」式的案件名称中，排在「诉」之后的那一方
senses.example: In the report the defendant appeared second in the case name.
senses.exampleCN: 在报道中，被告排在案件名称的第二位。
senses.why: Court practice fixes the order of names, and the second slot marks the party being complained against, a convention the word now encodes.
senses.whyCN: 法庭实务固定了名称顺序，第二个位置标记被投诉的一方，这个词如今就编码了这一惯例。

senses.title: A defender in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中的防守者、辩护者
senses.definition: in older texts, a person who defends a place, a cause or another person
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指守卫某地、某项事业或他人的人
senses.example: The chronicle names him as the defendant of the northern wall.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史称他为北墙的守卫者。
senses.why: Before it became a courtroom label, the participle simply meant the one defending, in war or in argument, and older writing keeps that sense.
senses.whyCN: 在成为法庭标签之前，这个分词只表示「正在防守的人」，无论战阵还是辩论，较早文本保留了这一含义。

senses.title: Anyone who must answer criticism
senses.definition: figuratively, a person or body put in the position of answering a public charge
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义上，被置于公开指控之下、必须作答的个人或机构
senses.example: The minister found himself the defendant in a public inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位部长发现自己在公开调查中成了被质询的一方。
senses.why: Because the legal frame is so familiar, it transfers to public argument, where the accused side must answer before an audience.
senses.whyCN: 因为法律框架太熟悉，它便转移到公共争论中：被指控的一方要在众人面前作答。

senses.title: The responding party in a tribunal
senses.titleCN: 仲裁或裁判庭中的应诉方
senses.definition: the party answering a claim in arbitration or an administrative tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 在仲裁或行政裁判庭中应对请求的一方
senses.example: The defendant in the arbitration agreed to a private hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁中的应诉方同意进行不公开听证。
senses.why: Courts are not the only forum, and the word travels to any body that hears a claim and expects an answer.
senses.whyCN: 法院并非唯一的场域，这个词也适用于任何受理请求并要求答辩的机构。

intro.en: Defendant is the Old French present participle of defendre, from Latin defendere 'to ward off'. The verb joins de- 'away' with fendere 'to strike', the same second element seen in offend. The deeper origin of fendere is source uncertain.
intro.cn: defendant 是古法语 defendre 的现在分词，源自拉丁 defendere「挡开」。这个动词由 de-「离开」与 fendere「击打」构成，后半与 offend 共享。fendere 的更深来源属来源不确定。

items.en: Fendere meant to strike or push. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the connections sometimes proposed for it are reconstructions rather than settled derivations.
items.cn: fendere 意为击打、推。其更深来源属来源不确定，偶尔为它提出的关联只是重构，并非已定的派生。

items.en: De- 'away' plus fendere gave defendere, 'to ward off, to repel, to protect'. The military image is a blow pushed aside.
items.cn: de-「离开」加 fendere 构成 defendere，意为挡开、击退、保护。军事意象是一记被推开的打击。

items.en: The same second element appears in offendere 'to strike against', the source of offend, which shows that fendere was a productive verb of striking.
items.cn: 同一个后半也出现在 offendere「撞击、冒犯」中，即 offend 的来源，说明 fendere 曾是一个能产的「击打」动词。

items.en: French defendre meant to defend, to protect and also to forbid, a range that English inherited in part through legal phrases.
items.cn: 法语 defendre 意为防守、保护，也意为禁止，这一范围部分经法律短语传入英语。

items.en: The present participle defendant meant 'the defending one' and was used as a noun in legal French for the party answering a charge.
items.cn: 现在分词 defendant 意为「正在辩护的那一个」，在法律法语中作名词，指对指控作出答辩的一方。

items.en: English dropped the military sense from ordinary speech and kept the procedural role, while the older idea survives in historical writing about defenders of a place.
items.cn: 英语在日常口语中丢掉了军事义，保住了程序角色；而「守卫某地者」的旧义仍留在历史文字里。

note.en: Group one separates the verb, the defender, the abstract case and a look-alike with a different source; group two sets the role against the other names used for people in a case.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词、防守者、抽象的案件名目，以及一个来源不同的形近词；第二组把这个角色与案中其他人的称呼作对照。

entries.definition: The act of answering a claim or protecting someone; the defendant is the person in that position.
entries.definitionCN: 指应对请求或保护他人的动作；defendant 是处于这个位置的人。

entries.definition: One who defends, often a protector; a defendant defends himself but is named by the claim against him.
entries.definitionCN: 指防守者，常含保护者意味；被告也为自己辩护，但他是按被指控的身份命名的。

entries.definition: The answer or the whole case for the accused; the defendant is the party, not the argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指答辩或被告方的整套主张；defendant 是当事方，不是论证本身。

entries.definition: Openly refusing to obey, from French defier 'to defy'; it looks like defendant but comes from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 公开拒绝服从，来自法语 defier「挑战、违抗」；外形像 defendant，却出自另一个动词。

entries.definition: The possessive form marking something belonging to the party, not a separate role.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，表示属于该当事方之物，不是另一个角色。

entries.definition: The person charged with a crime, common in criminal reporting; defendant is the procedural term in court.
entries.definitionCN: 被控犯罪的人，常用于犯罪报道；defendant 是法庭上的程序用语。

entries.definition: The party who answers in an appeal, arbitration or divorce case; defendant belongs to first-instance court language.
entries.definitionCN: 在上诉、仲裁或离婚案件中作答的一方；defendant 属于一审法庭的用语。

entries.definition: Any party to a lawsuit, claiming or answering; defendant names only the answering side.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中的任何一方，原告或被告皆可；defendant 只指应诉的一方。

entries.definition: The party who brings the civil claim, the mirror image of the defendant.
entries.definitionCN: 提起民事请求的一方，正是被告的镜像。

entries.definition: The party who appeals a decision; at that stage the old labels of plaintiff and defendant give way.
entries.definitionCN: 对判决提起上诉的一方；到了这一阶段，原告与被告的旧标签就让位了。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb of warding off and the real procedural opposites.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「挡开」动词，以及真实的程序对立体。

normal.en: Defendere is to push a blow away: the defendant is the one who must push the claim away.
normal.cn: defendere 是把打击推开：被告就是必须把请求推开的那个人。

normal.en: Offend and defend share the striking verb: one strikes against, the other strikes away.
normal.cn: offend 与 defend 共享「击打」动词：一个撞上去，一个挡开。

normal.en: Defender is the protector, defendant is the accused: the same verb, two directions of attention.
normal.cn: defender 是保护者，defendant 是被指控者：同一个动词，注意力朝向两个方向。

normal.en: Defiant is a look-alike: it comes from a verb meaning to defy, not from the verb of warding off.
normal.cn: defiant 是形近词：它出自意为「违抗」的动词，而不是「挡开」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the pair: plaintiff and defendant, the defendant's plea, a co-defendant.
normal.cn: 固定说法展示这对关系：原告与被告、被告的答辩、同案被告。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand catching a thrown object: the hand is the defendant's whole job.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手接住抛来的东西：这只手就是被告的全部工作。

abstract.en: Picture a name written second on a courtroom docket, after the versus.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭日程表上第二个写下的名字，位于「诉」字之后。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing while everyone else sits, answering a document held in one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象所有人都坐着，只有一个人站着，手里拿着文件作答。

examples.en: The defendant chose to remain silent and let the lawyer speak.
examples.cn: 被告选择保持沉默，由律师发言。

examples.en: A co-defendant agreed to testify against the others.
examples.cn: 一名同案被告同意作证指控其他人。

examples.en: The court reminded the defendant that the burden of proof had not shifted.
examples.cn: 法院提醒被告，举证责任并未转移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地防等」——站在被告席上，得就地防守、等着对方出招 → 被告

root: 古法语 defendant（defendre 的现在分词，意为「正在辩护的」），源自拉丁 defendere（挡开、保护）= de-（离开）+ fendere（击打）。fendere 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the criminal accused, through the civil party sued, the neutral answering side, the bearer of the burden, the second name in a case title, the old defender, the public figure answering criticism, and the responding party in arbitration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从刑事被告开始，经民事被诉方、中性的应诉方、承担答辩责任者、案件名称中的第二顺位、旧时的防守者、公开受质询者，最后到仲裁中的应诉方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised to catch a thrown object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手，接住抛来的东西。

branches.en: THE TWO COURTS: the same answering role serves criminal charges and civil claims.
branches.cn: 两类法庭：同一个应诉角色既服务于刑事指控，也服务于民事请求。

branches.en: THE NEUTRAL LABEL: procedure needs a name for the answering side that carries no hint of guilt.
branches.cn: 中性标签：程序需要一个不含罪责暗示的名称来指作答的一方。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: once a claim is filed, this party must produce evidence and argument.
branches.cn: 重量：请求一经提出，这一方就必须拿出证据与论证。

branches.en: THE ORDER OF NAMES: the second slot in a case title marks the party complained against.
branches.cn: 名称顺序：案件名称的第二格标记被投诉的一方。

branches.en: THE WIDER USE: the old defender, the public figure under criticism and the party in arbitration all keep the core of warding off a charge.
branches.cn: 更宽的用法：旧时的防守者、受公众指责的人物、仲裁中的应诉方，都保留「挡开指控」的内核。

intro.en: Defendant is a Latin participle used as a noun, so its ending marks the person in the act of defending.
intro.cn: defendant 是作名词使用的拉丁分词，词尾标记正在辩护的那个人。

latinIntro.en: The verb defendere is de- 'away' plus fendere 'to strike'; the present participle defendens supplies the English form, and the same striking verb also built offend.
latinIntro.cn: 动词 defendere 是 de-「离开」加 fendere「击打」；现在分词 defendens 提供英语形态，同一个「击打」动词也构成了 offend。

items.meaningCN: 离开、去掉（前缀表示把东西推开）
items.example: The prefix points the blow away from the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把打击指向身体之外。

items.meaningCN: 挡开；保护（把打击推离自身）
items.example: The compound named the warding off.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词命名「挡开」。

items.meaningCN: 正在防守的（分词词尾标记动作进行中）
items.example: The participle named the one defending.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词命名正在防守的人。

items.structure: defendant (French participle used as a noun)
items.meaningCN: 对指控作答的人（分词名词化，由动作转为角色）
正在做某事的人（分词词尾把动作转成施事者）
items.example: A claimant is one who claims.
items.exampleCN: claimant 就是提出请求的人。

items.meaningCN: 答辩；防御（抽象名词词尾把动作转成事体）
防守者；保护者（英语施事后缀，与 -ant 的「被控方」形成对照）
items.example: The defender of the fort surrendered.

definition_zh: 诉讼；诉讼程序；（总称）打官司
definition_en: the process of taking a dispute to a court and arguing it there, or the cases so handled
core_image: 两个人隔着长桌，把同一件事的两种说法各装进文件盒，盒子越堆越高，走廊越走越长
scene: 两家公司为一项专利争了多年，文件盒在会议室里堆到墙边。 Years of litigation drained the budget before any ruling came.
sceneCN: 这里 litigation 指持续多年的诉讼过程（第 2 个义项：官司从立案到裁决的漫长进行）；句意：在裁决到来之前，多年的诉讼已经耗尽了预算。图中可辨识物件：文件盒、长桌、专利证书、堆叠的卷宗。

pos.zh: 诉讼；诉讼程序（通常作不可数名词，指活动或整体；指多批案件时偶用复数）

forms.label: 复数（专业语境偶见，通常不可数）

senses.title: The machinery of suing
senses.definition: the system and steps by which a dispute is brought before a court
senses.definitionCN: 把争议提交法院的系统与步骤
senses.example: The contract sends any disagreement straight into litigation.
senses.exampleCN: 合同把任何分歧直接送进诉讼程序。
senses.why: The noun names the activity rather than one case, because it is built from the verb of going to law plus the suffix of action.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由「去打官司」的动词加表动作的后缀构成，所以它指活动本身，而不是某一桩案件。

senses.title: The long running of a case
senses.titleCN: 官司从立案到裁决的漫长进行
senses.definition: the drawn-out course of a contested case through pleadings, hearings and appeal
senses.definitionCN: 有争议案件经答辩、开庭与上诉的漫长过程
senses.example: Years of litigation drained the budget before any ruling came.
senses.exampleCN: 在裁决到来之前，多年的诉讼已经耗尽了预算。
senses.why: Because the word is uncountable, it easily measures duration: litigation can go on, drag on, or finally end.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词不可数，它天然适合计量时间：诉讼可以持续、拖延，也可以终于结束。

senses.title: A field of legal practice
senses.definition: the branch of legal work concerned with contested cases
senses.definitionCN: 法律工作中处理争议案件的那一支
senses.example: She moved from tax advice into commercial litigation.
senses.exampleCN: 她从税务咨询转到了商业诉讼。
senses.why: Once the activity is regular, it becomes a speciality with its own skills, so the word turns into the name of a practice area.
senses.whyCN: 活动一旦常规化，就会形成有专门技能的分支，于是这个词变成了执业领域的名称。

senses.title: The volume of cases
senses.titleCN: 诉讼案件的数量或诉讼潮
senses.definition: the amount of court business generated by disputes in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内由争议产生的法院案件量
senses.example: Cheap filing fees produced a wave of litigation against landlords.
senses.exampleCN: 低廉的立案费引发了一波针对房东的诉讼。
senses.why: An uncountable activity can still be counted in bulk, as a wave or a flood, which is how the word reports case volume.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的活动仍可按规模来计数，如一波、一股洪流，这个词就是这样报告案件量的。

senses.title: The road not taken: no settlement
senses.definition: the choice to fight a case in court rather than settle it
senses.definitionCN: 选择在法院争到底而不是和解
senses.example: The board chose litigation over a quiet settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会选择诉讼，而不是低调和解。
senses.why: Negotiation ends the dispute privately; litigation moves it into a public forum with a third party deciding, so the two are named as opposites.
senses.whyCN: 谈判私下结束争议；诉讼则把它搬进公开场合，由第三方裁决，所以两者被当作对立的两条路。

senses.title: The bill for fighting
senses.definition: the cost, delay and disruption that contested cases impose
senses.definitionCN: 争议案件带来的费用、拖延与干扰
senses.example: The fear of litigation keeps small clinics from hiring specialists.
senses.exampleCN: 对诉讼的恐惧让小型诊所不敢聘用专科医生。
senses.why: Because the noun names the whole activity, it can stand for its price: lawyers, years and lost attention all fold into one word.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指整个活动，它也能代表代价：律师费、年份与被耗掉的精力都折进这一个词里。

senses.title: The act of pressing a claim
senses.titleCN: 提起并推进请求的行为
senses.definition: the deliberate act of pursuing a claim through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 有意通过法院追究某项请求的行为
senses.example: Litigation was the only way left to recover the deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 提起诉讼是追回押金的唯一办法。
senses.why: The same noun covers the single decision to sue, because the act and the institution share one name.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也覆盖「决定去告」这一步，因为动作与制度共用了一个名字。

senses.title: The institution of contested justice
senses.titleCN: 以对抗方式解决争议的制度
senses.definition: the adversarial system itself, seen as one way among several to resolve disputes
senses.definitionCN: 对抗式解决争议的制度本身，被视为多种方式之一
senses.example: Comparative studies ask why some societies rely on litigation and others on mediation.
senses.exampleCN: 比较研究追问：为何有些社会倚重诉讼，另一些倚重调解。
senses.why: Zoom out far enough and the activity becomes a social institution, which societies may use more or less than mediation and arbitration.
senses.whyCN: 拉远看，这项活动就成了一种社会制度，各社会对它的倚重程度可以高于或低于调解与仲裁。

intro.en: Litigation comes from Latin litigatio, the action noun of litigare 'to go to law'. Litigare itself joins lis 'dispute' to agere 'to drive, do'. The deeper origin of lis is unsettled.
intro.cn: litigation 来自拉丁 litigatio，是 litigare「去打官司」的动作名词；litigare 由 lis「争执」加 agere「驱动、做」构成。lis 更深来源没有定论。

items.en: Lis (genitive litis) meant a dispute, a quarrel or a lawsuit. Its deeper origin is source uncertain: the Indo-European forms sometimes offered for it are reconstructions, and no single etymology is established.
items.cn: lis（属格 litis）指争执、口角或诉讼。其更深来源属来源不确定：有时为它给出的印欧语形式都是重构形式，没有哪一条词源得到确证。

items.en: Agere meant to drive, to set in motion, and also to do or to plead a case. It is the source of act, agent, agenda and exact, and here it supplies the 'carrying on' of a dispute.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、使运动，也指做某事或在庭上陈述。它是 act、agent、agenda、exact 的来源，在这里提供「把争执一路推下去」的意思。

items.en: Lis plus agere produced litigare, 'to dispute, to go to law, to plead'. The verb describes both quarrelling and carrying the quarrel into court.
items.cn: lis 加 agere 构成 litigare，意为「争执、诉诸法院、在庭上陈述」。这个动词既指争吵，也指把争吵带进法院。

items.en: Litigatio, the action noun, named the proceeding itself. English took the stem through French legal usage in the seventeenth century, keeping the abstract, uncountable sense.
items.cn: 动作名词 litigatio 指诉讼程序本身。英语经法语法律用语在十七世纪借入这个词干，保留了抽象、不可数的用法。

items.en: Modern usage splits the field into civil and commercial litigation, and treats litigation as the alternative to settlement, mediation or arbitration; the plural appears only when separate batches of cases are meant.
items.cn: 现代用法把这一领域分为民事诉讼与商业诉讼，并把诉讼视为和解、调解、仲裁之外的另一种选择；只有指多批案件时才用复数。

note.en: Group one holds relatives built on the same lis stem plus two dangerous near-words; group two holds other ways of naming a legal proceeding.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 lis 词干的亲属词，外加两个极易误认的近词；第二组是称呼法律程序的其他说法。

entries.definition: The verb of the same stem: to contest a matter in court, not the activity as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干的动词：在法院争讼，而不是指整项活动。

entries.definition: A party to a case; the -ant suffix marks the one doing, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 案件的一方；-ant 后缀标记做事的人，而不是事情本身。

entries.definition: Fond of suing, or relating to lawsuits; the -ous suffix turns the activity into a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 好打官司的，或与诉讼有关的；-ous 后缀把活动变成一种性情。

entries.definition: Lawmaking, from lex 'law' plus latio 'a bringing'; it is close in sound to litigation but shares no stem.
entries.definitionCN: 立法，由 lex「法律」加 latio「带来」构成；读音与 litigation 相近，却没有共同词干。

entries.definition: A repeated prayer or a long list, from Greek litaneia 'supplication'; the opening letters match but the source does not.
entries.definitionCN: 连祷或一长串清单，来自希腊 litaneia「恳求」；开头字母相同，来源却不同。

entries.definition: A single civil case with a number; litigation is the activity those cases make up.
entries.definitionCN: 有编号的单件民事案件；litigation 是这些案件构成的活动。

entries.definition: The formal steps recorded in a case, or the record of them; more procedural, less combative.
entries.definitionCN: 案件中记录在案的形式步骤或其记录；更偏程序，对抗色彩较淡。

entries.definition: Dispute resolution before a private arbitrator rather than a court; often named as the alternative to litigation.
entries.definitionCN: 由私人仲裁员而非法院解决争议，常被视为诉讼之外的替代方式。

entries.definition: The formal British name for a civil suit; it points to one case rather than to the whole activity.
entries.definitionCN: 英式正式说法，指一件民事诉讼；它指向单件案件，而不是整个活动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin stems, the real word family and the fixed phrases of practice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词干、真实的同族词与实务中的固定说法。

normal.en: Lis 'dispute' plus agere 'drive': to drive a dispute forward is to litigate.
normal.cn: lis「争执」加 agere「驱动」：把争执一路推下去，就是打官司。

normal.en: The family runs litigate, litigant, litigator, litigious and relitigate, all on the same stem.
normal.cn: 同族词有 litigate、litigant、litigator、litigious 与 relitigate，全在同一词干上。

normal.en: Legislation looks and sounds close, but it is lex plus latio, lawmaking, not case-fighting.
normal.cn: legislation 形音都近，却由 lex 加 latio 构成，指立法，不是打官司。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: civil litigation, commercial litigation, litigation costs.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：民事诉讼、商业诉讼、诉讼费用。

normal.en: The word is normally uncountable, so it behaves like water: a wave of litigation, years of litigation.
normal.cn: 这个词通常不可数，行为像水：一波诉讼、多年诉讼。

abstract.en: Picture two people pushing the same heavy box from opposite ends down a corridor that has no exit.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人从两端推同一只重箱子，走在一条没有出口的走廊上。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that only bills by the year, never by the hour: that is how litigation measures time.
abstract.cn: 想象一只只按年计费、从不按小时计费的钟：诉讼就是这样计量时间的。

abstract.en: Picture a public stage where a private quarrel must be performed in costume before a stranger decides how it ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个公开舞台，私人的口角必须穿着戏服演一遍，再由陌生人决定它怎么结束。

examples.en: The insurer set aside a fund for litigation over the collapsed bridge.
examples.cn: 保险公司为垮桥一事的诉讼预留了一笔资金。

examples.en: Most disputes never reach litigation because the cost is known in advance.
examples.cn: 多数争议从未进入诉讼，因为费用事先就清楚了。

examples.en: She built a career in environmental litigation.
examples.cn: 她在环境诉讼领域建立了事业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立案＋跟踪」——案子立了还要一路跟下去，跟得越久越像一场马拉松 → 诉讼

root: 拉丁 litigare（争执、诉诸法院）= lis（争执）+ agere（驱动、做）；动作名词 litigatio。lis 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the procedure, through its duration, its trade and its volume, to the choice against settlement, its price, the single act of suing and finally the institution itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从程序本身，经它的时长、行业与案件量，走到与和解相对的选择、它的代价、一次起诉的动作，最后落到制度层面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quarrel turned into files, pushed down a corridor that keeps getting longer.
core.cn: 核心意象：争执被变成卷宗，沿一条不断变长的走廊被推下去。

branches.en: THE MACHINERY AND ITS CLOCK: the steps exist, and because they are steps they take years.
branches.cn: 机器与它的时钟：步骤存在，而正因为是步骤，它就要花上几年。

branches.en: THE TRADE: repeated steps become a skill that people practise for a living.
branches.cn: 行业：重复的步骤变成一门可以赖以为生的手艺。

branches.en: SCALE AND CHOICE: cases can arrive in waves, and each dispute is either fought here or settled elsewhere.
branches.cn: 规模与选择：案件可以成波涌来，而每桩争议要么在这里争，要么在别处和解。

branches.en: THE PRICE: the same activity that takes years also takes money, attention and nerve.
branches.cn: 代价：耗掉年份的活动，也耗掉钱、精力与胆量。

branches.en: FROM ONE ACT TO A SYSTEM: one decision to sue is the same shape as a whole society's way of deciding disputes.
branches.cn: 从一个动作到一个制度：一次起诉的决定，与整个社会解决争议的方式是同一个形状。

intro.en: Litigation is built from a Latin noun of dispute, a Latin verb of driving, and an English action suffix, so it can be read stem by stem.
intro.cn: litigation 由拉丁的争执名词、拉丁的驱动动词与英语的动作后缀构成，可以按词干逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin lis gives litigate, litigant, litigator, litigious and relitigate; Latin agere separately gives act, agent, agenda and exact, which is why the two families look unrelated in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lis 衍生 litigate、litigant、litigator、litigious 与 relitigate；拉丁 agere 另自衍生 act、agent、agenda、exact，所以两族在英语里看起来毫不相干。

items.meaning: a dispute, a quarrel, a lawsuit
items.example: The stem carries the quarrel itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载争执本身。

items.structure: agere, egi, actum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.meaning: to drive, to do, to plead
items.example: The verb supplies the pushing forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「往前推」的意思。

items.meaning: to go to law, to plead a case
items.example: They chose to litigate rather than settle.
items.exampleCN: 他们选择打官司而不是和解。

items.meaning: the activity of contesting cases in court
items.meaningCN: 在法院争讼的活动（动作后缀把动词变成抽象活动）
items.exampleCN: 诉讼可以比发起它的人活得更久。

items.meaning: a lawyer who fights cases in court
items.meaningCN: 在法院打案的律师（施事后缀把活动变成从事者）
items.example: The litigator prepared for a long trial.
items.exampleCN: 这位诉讼律师为一场长审做准备。

items.meaningCN: 案件当事方（分词后缀把活动变成正在其中的人）

items.meaning: given to suing; relating to suits
items.meaningCN: 好打官司的；与诉讼相关的（形容词后缀把活动变成性情）
items.example: A litigious neighbour can exhaust a small firm.
items.exampleCN: 一个好打官司的邻居能把小公司拖垮。

items.meaning: to fight the same issue again
items.meaningCN: 就同一争点再打一次官司（重复前缀把动作加一轮）
items.example: The court refused to relitigate the issue.
items.exampleCN: 法院拒绝再审这一争点。

definition_zh: n. 仲裁，公断（由中立第三方裁断争议）；（合同中的）仲裁机制
definition_en: The settlement of a dispute by an independent third party whose decision the sides have agreed to accept; in contracts, the mechanism that replaces going to court.
core_image: 双方各说各话，交给中间那个人拍板
scene: 合同写明争议一律提交仲裁。 The contract sends every dispute to arbitration.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arbitration 指把争议交给中立第三方裁断，而不是上法院。

senses.title: Settlement by a third party
senses.definition: the process in which a neutral person or panel hears both sides and issues a decision that resolves the dispute
senses.definitionCN: 由中立个人或小组听取双方陈述并作出解决争议的裁定的程序
senses.example: The pay dispute ended in arbitration after six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 六周之后，薪酬争议以仲裁收场。
senses.why: The root arbiter means one who goes to see and judge, so arbitration is literally the work of that witness turned judge.
senses.whyCN: 词根 arbiter 意为「去看并作出判断的人」，所以 arbitration 字面就是那位见证人转为裁判后所做的工作。

senses.title: The contractual mechanism
senses.definition: in law and commerce, the agreed route that replaces litigation, usually written into a contract as a clause
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与商业中，指替代诉讼的约定途径，通常以条款形式写进合同
senses.example: Binding arbitration bars either side from suing later.
senses.exampleCN: 有约束力的仲裁禁止任何一方事后起诉。
senses.why: Here the word names an institution rather than an event: the standing arrangement the parties chose before any quarrel began.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指的是一套制度而非一次事件：双方在争吵开始之前就选好的常设安排。

intro.en: Arbitration comes from Latin arbitratio, from arbitrari, to judge, from arbiter, a witness who goes to see, built from ad-, to, and baetere, to come.
intro.cn: arbitration 来自拉丁语 arbitratio，出自 arbitrari「裁断」，而 arbitrari 来自 arbiter「去看情况的见证人」，由 ad-「向」与 baetere「来、去」构成。

items.en: Latin arbiter named someone who goes to look at a matter and then judges it, a witness with authority.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arbiter 指去查看某事然后作出判断的人，一个有权威的见证人。

items.en: The verb arbitrari meant to consider and decide, at first neutrally, without any hint of whim.
items.cn: 动词 arbitrari 意为「考量并裁定」，起初是中性的，没有任何「随意」的意味。

items.en: The noun arbitratio named the act of judging between parties, the source of the modern term.
items.cn: 名词 arbitratio 指在各方之间裁断这一行为，是现代术语的来源。

items.en: Old French kept arbitration for settlement out of court, a practice medieval merchants relied on.
items.cn: 古法语用 arbitration 指庭外解决，这是中世纪商人依赖的做法。

items.en: English recorded the word in the fourteenth century for the decision of an arbitrator.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪记录该词，指仲裁人作出的裁定。

items.en: Today arbitration clauses sit in trade and labour contracts, and the award is enforceable across borders.
items.cn: 如今仲裁条款见于贸易与劳动合同，裁决可跨境执行。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts arbitrary, which is whim rather than reasoned judgement, and arbitrage, a trading term; the near-meaning group lists other ways to settle a dispute.
note.cn: 形近组对比 arbitrary「凭兴致而非讲理裁断」与 arbitrage「套利」；近义组列出其他解决争议的方式。

entries.definition: Based on whim, not on reason.
entries.definitionCN: 凭兴致而非依理。

entries.definition: To judge between two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 在双方之间裁断。

entries.definition: A person with power to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 有权作出裁定的人。

entries.definition: Profiting from price gaps between markets.
entries.definitionCN: 利用市场间价差获利。

entries.definition: Helping sides reach their own deal.
entries.definitionCN: 帮双方自行达成协议。

entries.definition: A formal ruling on a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 对争议的正式裁定。

entries.definition: Bringing hostile parties together.
entries.definitionCN: 使对立双方和解。

entries.definition: An agreement that ends a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 结束争议的协议。

normalIntro.en: Arbitration is arbiter plus -ation: the work of the person who comes, looks and decides.
normalIntro.cn: arbitration 就是 arbiter 加 -ation：那位「来看一看再拍板」的人所做的工作。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say arbitration, not an arbitration.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 arbitration，不说 an arbitration。

normal.en: The person is an arbitrator; the verb is arbitrate.
normal.cn: 人是 arbitrator，动词是 arbitrate。

normal.en: Arbitrary means capricious, a very different judgement.
normal.cn: arbitrary 意为反复无常，是完全不同的评价。

normal.en: Mediation helps sides agree; arbitration decides for them.
normal.cn: mediation 帮双方谈成，arbitration 替他们定。

normal.en: The result is called an award, not a verdict.
normal.cn: 结果叫 award，不叫 verdict。

abstract.en: Picture two people pointing at one line on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两人指着地图上同一条线争执。

abstract.en: Imagine a third chair placed between two arguing sides.
abstract.cn: 想象在争执双方之间摆上第三把椅子。

abstract.en: Think of a contract that quietly rules out court.
abstract.cn: 想象一份悄悄排除法院的合同。

examples.en: Both firms agreed to settle by arbitration.
examples.cn: 两家公司同意通过仲裁解决。

examples.en: The arbitration clause survives the rest of the contract.
examples.cn: 仲裁条款在合同其余部分失效后仍然有效。

examples.en: Arbitration is usually faster than a court case.
examples.cn: 仲裁通常比诉讼快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arbiter「裁判」+ -ation「行为」——请裁判来断案，就是仲裁 arbitration。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 baetere「来」成 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」，生出 arbitrari「裁断」与 arbitratio；经古法语入英语作 arbitration，指庭外裁断。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one act of judging: the hearing that settles a quarrel, and the standing arrangement that promises such a hearing.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种裁断：解决争吵的那次听审，以及承诺会有这种听审的常设安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sides talking past each other, one person in the middle deciding
core.cn: 核心意象：双方各说各话，交给中间那个人拍板

branches.en: A pay quarrel closed in six weeks.
branches.cn: 六周结束的薪酬争议。

branches.en: A panel hearing both sides once.
branches.cn: 一次性听取双方的小组。

branches.en: A clause that rules out court.
branches.cn: 排除法院的条款。

branches.en: An award enforceable abroad.
branches.cn: 可在境外执行的裁决。

branches.en: Both put the decision in a third hand.
branches.cn: 两者都把裁定交到第三方手里。

intro.en: Arbitration is arbiter plus -ation; the same root builds arbitrate, arbitrator, arbitral, arbitrary and arbitrage.
intro.cn: arbitration 是 arbiter 加 -ation；同一词根还构成 arbitrate、arbitrator、arbitral、arbitrary 与 arbitrage。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arbiter, arbitrari and arbitratio; the prefix inside arbiter is ad-, to, before baetere, to come.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arbiter、arbitrari 与 arbitratio；arbiter 内部的前缀是 ad-「向」，接 baetere「来」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arbitrari 是 arbitration 的来源。

definition_zh: 管辖权；管辖范围；（法院或机关的）受理权限；司法管辖
definition_en: the official power of a court or authority to hear cases, make decisions or regulate a field, and the area or matters over which that power applies
core_image: 河岸上立着一块界碑，两名警官各自站在自己这一侧，谁都不肯把脚跨过去
scene: 两名警官在河边争执，却谁也不肯跨过界碑，因为那段水面不在自己的辖区之内。 Neither officer would cross the boundary stone, because the stretch of water lay outside his jurisdiction.
sceneCN: 这里 jurisdiction 指「某一机关有权处理的地域范围」（第 2 个义项：管辖区域）；句意为两名警官都不肯跨过界碑，因为那段水面不在自己的辖区之内。图中可辨识物件：界碑、河水、警徽、两岸的标记。

pos.zh: 管辖权；管辖范围；受理权限

derivatives.zh: 法学家（同出 ius，但不指权限）

senses.title: A court's power to hear a case
senses.titleCN: 法院受理与审判案件的权限
senses.definition: the power of a court to hear a particular kind of case and give a binding decision
senses.definitionCN: 法院受理某一类案件并作出有约束力决定的权力
senses.example: The appeal failed because the tribunal had no jurisdiction over criminal matters.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉失败，因为该裁判所对刑事事项没有管辖权。
senses.why: The word joins ius 'law' to dictio 'a saying': jurisdiction is literally the speaking of law, and only certain courts are granted the right to speak it over certain cases.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 ius「法」与 dictio「宣告」结合起来：管辖权字面上就是「宣告法律」，而只有特定法院被授予就特定案件宣告法律的资格。

senses.title: The area covered
senses.definition: the geographical area within which an authority may act
senses.definitionCN: 某一机关可以行动的地理范围
senses.example: Neither officer would cross the boundary stone, because the stretch of water lay outside his jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警官都不肯跨过界碑，因为那段水面不在自己的辖区之内。
senses.why: Power needs a where as well as a what, so the abstract right is measured onto land, and the boundary becomes the visible form of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 权力既需要「对什么」，也需要「在哪里」，于是抽象权限被丈量到土地上，界线成了这个名词可见的形态。

senses.title: Regulatory power over a field
senses.titleCN: 对某一领域的监管权限
senses.definition: the authority of a public body to set and enforce rules in a particular sector
senses.definitionCN: 公共机构在某一行业设定并执行规则的权力
senses.example: Energy pricing fell within the jurisdiction of the provincial board.
senses.exampleCN: 能源定价属于省委员会的管辖范围。
senses.why: Modern regulators hold powers that were once judicial, and they describe their remit with the same noun because both mean the right to decide authoritatively.
senses.whyCN: 现代监管机构握有曾经属于司法的权力，它们用同一个名词来描述职权范围，因为两者都指权威地作出决定的资格。

senses.title: A state's legal power
senses.titleCN: 国家对人与地的法律权力
senses.definition: the legal competence of a state over persons, property and events connected with its territory
senses.definitionCN: 国家对与其领土相关的人、财产与事件的法律权限
senses.example: The ship was seized in waters under national jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 该船在受国家管辖的水域被扣押。
senses.why: Sovereignty and jurisdiction are not the same: a state may own nothing in a place and still hold the right to try crimes committed there.
senses.whyCN: 主权与管辖权并不相同：一个国家可以在某地没有任何产业，却仍拥有审判在那里发生的罪行的权力。

senses.title: The limits of any authority
senses.titleCN: 任何权限的边界（在权限内/越权）
senses.definition: the scope within which a person or body may properly act, often invoked when someone has gone beyond it
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某机构可以正当行动的界限，常在有人越界时被援引
senses.example: The inspector was told that the question lay outside her jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 有人告知这位稽查员，该问题超出她的权限。
senses.why: The noun is used negatively as much as positively: saying that something is outside a jurisdiction is the standard way to refuse to act.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词的否定用法与肯定用法一样多：说某事「不在管辖之内」，是拒绝行动的惯常说法。

senses.title: Competence between states
senses.titleCN: 国际法上国家之间的管辖权限
senses.definition: the competence of one state to exercise authority, especially criminal jurisdiction, over acts with a foreign element
senses.definitionCN: 一国对有外国因素的行为行使权威（尤其是刑事管辖）的权限
senses.example: Under universal jurisdiction, any state may try the case.
senses.exampleCN: 依普遍管辖权，任何国家都可以审理该案。
senses.why: Where there is no world court, the noun is used to divide competence between sovereigns, and the dividing line is negotiated rather than drawn by a single legislator.
senses.whyCN: 在没有世界法院的地方，这个名词用来在主权国家之间划分权限，而那条分界线是协商出来的，并非由单一立法者画出。

senses.title: The authority of a church court
senses.definition: the power of an ecclesiastical court or bishop to decide matters of doctrine and discipline
senses.definitionCN: 教会法庭或主教就教义与纪律事项作出决定的权力
senses.example: The marriage case was returned to the church's own jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩婚姻案件被交回教会自己的管辖范围。
senses.why: Church courts held this power long before royal ones, so the noun entered legal language with an ecclesiastical owner already in place.
senses.whyCN: 教会法庭掌握这项权力远早于王室法庭，因此这个名词进入法律语言时，早已有一个教会的所有者。

senses.title: Exercising or declining it
senses.titleCN: 行使或拒绝行使管辖权
senses.definition: the act by which a court takes up a matter, or formally refuses to
senses.definitionCN: 法院接手某一事项、或正式拒绝接手的动作
senses.example: The court declined jurisdiction and left the parties to arbitrate.
senses.exampleCN: 法院拒绝行使管辖权，让当事人自行仲裁。
senses.why: Rights are exercised by acts, so the noun also names the moment of taking or refusing a case, which is why lawyers speak of assuming and declining jurisdiction.
senses.whyCN: 权利通过行为行使，因此这个名词也命名接手或拒绝案件的时刻，律师所谓「取得管辖」与「拒绝管辖」即由此而来。

intro.en: Jurisdiction comes from Latin iurisdictio, from ius 'law, right' plus dictio 'a saying', from dicere 'to speak'. It entered English through French in the medieval period.
intro.cn: jurisdiction 来自拉丁 iurisdictio，由 ius「法、权利」加 dictio「宣告」（出自 dicere「说」）构成。它在中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ius meant law in the sense of right and binding custom, as distinct from lex, an enacted statute; the distinction matters for this word's relatives.
items.cn: ius 指作为权利与有约束力习俗的法，与 lex「被制定的法令」相区别；这一区别对这个词的同族词很重要。

items.en: Dicere meant to say or to declare publicly; dictio is the act of saying, so the compound names the public declaration of what is right.
items.cn: dicere 意为说、公开宣告；dictio 是「说」这一行为，因此这个复合词命名对何者为正当的公开宣告。

items.en: Iurisdictio in Roman law meant the magistrate's function of stating the law for a case, not the whole power of a modern court.
items.cn: iurisdictio 在罗马法中指长官为一案宣告法律这一职能，而非现代法院的全部权力。

items.en: Medieval church and royal courts both claimed the right to declare the law in their own spheres, and the noun was fixed to that division of competence.
items.cn: 中世纪教会法庭与王室法庭都主张在各自领域宣告法律的资格，这个名词被固定到这种权限划分上。

items.en: Modern states extended the noun to regulators and to international competence, so the word now covers any bounded right to decide.
items.cn: 现代国家把这个名词扩展到监管机构与国际权限，如今它覆盖任何有边界的决定权。

items.en: The English first date is approximate: the borrowing is medieval, but the earliest citation in legal French and English is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 英语首见年代为约数：借入发生在中世纪，但法律法语与英语中的最早书证没有精确年代。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin ius but differs in what it names; the second group names neighbouring kinds of authority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁 ius，但命名的对象不同；第二组是相邻的权限种类。

entries.definition: The adjective for anything concerning jurisdiction, especially in procedural objections.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与管辖权有关的事项，尤用于程序异议。

entries.definition: A scholar of law, from ius; it names a person who studies law, not a power.
entries.definitionCN: 法学家，出自 ius；它指研究法律的人，而非一种权力。

entries.definition: The theory or study of law, from ius plus prudentia 'knowledge'; it names learning, not the right to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 关于法的理论或研究，由 ius 加 prudentia「知识」构成；命名学问，而非决定权。

entries.definition: From iurare 'to swear', not ius: a sworn body of citizens, so its resemblance to jurisdiction is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 iurare「宣誓」而非 ius：指宣誓的公民团体，因此与 jurisdiction 的相似是假象。

entries.definition: From iudex, built on ius plus dicere, a cousin of the same stock but naming the person.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 iudex，由 ius 与 dicere 构成，同源但命名的是那个人。

entries.definition: Any recognised power to act or decide, with no territorial or subject limit built in.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被承认的行动或决定权，不含地域或事项的固有界限。

entries.definition: In law and diplomacy, the capacity of a body to act; it overlaps with jurisdiction but stresses capacity rather than territory.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律与外交中，指机构行事的能力；与 jurisdiction 重叠，但强调能力而非地域。

entries.definition: The locality where a case is tried, a question of convenience rather than of power.
entries.definitionCN: 审判案件的地点，属便利问题，而非权力问题。

entries.definition: The commission given to a body by a superior authority, which defines what it may do.
entries.definitionCN: 上级授予某机构的任务与权限，界定它可以做什么。

entries.definition: The scope of a statute or document, a matter of coverage rather than of power.
entries.definitionCN: 法令或文书的覆盖范围，属涵盖问题而非权力问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin law and saying, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「法」与「宣告」、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Ius is law and dictio is a saying, so jurisdiction is the saying of law, the right to declare it in a given case.
normal.cn: ius 是法，dictio 是宣告，因此管辖就是「宣告法律」，即就某一案件宣告法律的资格。

normal.en: The family runs jurisdiction, jurisdictional, jurisdictionally, jurist and jurisprudence.
normal.cn: 同族词有 jurisdiction、jurisdictional、jurisdictionally、jurist 与 jurisprudence。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the limits: within the jurisdiction of, outside the court's jurisdiction, exercise jurisdiction over.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出界限：在……管辖之内、超出法院管辖、对……行使管辖。

normal.en: Ius and lex were different words in Latin: the first is right, the second is statute, which is why jurisdiction and legal do not share a root.
normal.cn: 拉丁语中 ius 与 lex 是两个词：前者是权利，后者是法令，因此 jurisdiction 与 legal 并不同根。

normal.en: A boundary stone is the noun made visible, since every power needs a where.
normal.cn: 界碑是这个名词的可见形态，因为每一种权力都需要一个「在哪里」。

abstract.en: Picture two officers standing on either side of a stone, each unwilling to lift a foot.
abstract.cn: 想象两名警官站在界碑两侧，谁都不肯抬脚。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone that only works inside one room, however loud the speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象一支只在某个房间内起作用的麦克风，无论说话多大声。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut for one door in a street of identical doors.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，只配得上同一条街上众多相同门中的一扇。

examples.en: The case was moved to a court with proper jurisdiction.
examples.cn: 该案被移送到有适当管辖权的法院。

examples.en: Local police have no jurisdiction beyond the county line.
examples.cn: 地方警察在县界之外没有管辖权。

examples.en: The treaty allows jurisdiction to be shared in cross-border cases.
examples.cn: 该条约允许在跨境案件中共享管辖权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「juris（法）+ diction（宣告）」——有权宣告法律的范围 → 管辖权

root: 拉丁 ius「法、权利」+ dictio「宣告」（出自 dicere「说」）→ iurisdictio「宣告法律、司法职能」→ 法语 → 英语 jurisdiction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one boundary stone: it marks a court's cases, a district's ground, a regulator's sector, a state's reach, any authority's limit, the line between nations, a church's sphere, and the moment of taking or refusing a case.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一块界碑：它标出法院能审的案件、地区的土地、监管者的行业、国家的触及范围、任何权限的界限、国家之间的线、教会的领域，以及接手或拒绝案件的时刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone in the ground with an officer on either side, neither crossing.
core.cn: 核心意象：地上立着一块石头，两侧各有一名警官，谁都不越过去。

branches.en: POWER AND ITS EXERCISE: the right to hear and the act of taking a case are the same power asleep and awake.
branches.cn: 权力与行使：受理资格与接手案件的动作，是同一权力的睡与醒。

branches.en: THREE MAPS: a district, an industry and a state all draw the same boundary at different scales.
branches.cn: 三张地图：地区、行业与国家在不同尺度上画出同一条界线。

branches.en: THE LIMIT AS A REFUSAL: the noun is most often used to say that something is not mine to decide.
branches.cn: 界限即拒绝：这个名词最常用来表示「此事不归我决定」。

branches.en: BETWEEN SOVEREIGNS: without a world legislature, competence is negotiated rather than granted.
branches.cn: 主权之间：没有世界立法者，权限靠协商而非授予。

branches.en: THE OLDER COURT: a church court holds the same right to declare, and the noun needs no change.
branches.cn: 更早的法庭：教会法庭握有同样的宣告权，名词无需改动。

intro.en: Jurisdiction is a Latin compound of 'law' and 'saying', and both halves remain visible in English relatives.
intro.cn: jurisdiction 是拉丁语「法」与「宣告」的复合，两半在英语同族词里仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius gives jurist, jurisprudence and justice; dicere gives dictate, diction and verdict; the compound iurisdictio gives jurisdiction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ius 提供 jurist、jurisprudence 与 justice；dicere 提供 dictate、diction 与 verdict；复合词 iurisdictio 给出 jurisdiction。

items.example: The first half supplies law as right.
items.exampleCN: 前半提供作为权利的法。

items.example: The second half supplies the public saying.

items.meaning: the power to hear and decide

items.example: It appears in cognate nouns of similar shape.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在形状相近的同源名词中。

items.example: It builds jurisprudence, the study rather than the power.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 jurisprudence，指学问而非权力。

definition_zh: 规章；规则；管理；调控；调节
definition_en: an official rule, or the act of controlling and adjusting how something operates
core_image: 一只调速器在蒸汽机上方旋转，把过快的轮子压回稳定转速
scene: 工厂里贴出新通知：排放数据必须定期上报。 New regulation requires factories to report their emissions every quarter.
