sceneCN: 这里 regulation 指「具有约束力的规章」（第 1 个义项：官方制定的规则）；句意：新规章要求工厂每月报告排放。图中可辨识物件：法规文本、印章、排放烟囱、月度报表。

pos.zh: 规章；规则；管理；调控；（生物）调节；（欧洲联盟法）条例

senses.title: An official rule
senses.titleCN: 官方规章：具有约束力的规则
senses.definition: a rule made by a government or authority and binding on those it covers
senses.definitionCN: 由政府或主管机构制定、对其覆盖对象具有约束力的规则
senses.example: New regulation requires factories to report emissions every month.
senses.exampleCN: 新规章要求工厂每月报告排放。
senses.why: Regulation comes from Latin regula 'rule, straight stick', the same measure used to keep a line true; a rule keeps behaviour straight.
senses.whyCN: regulation 出自拉丁 regula「规则、直木条」，即用来把线画直的量尺；规则的作用正是把行为「拉直」。

senses.title: Government oversight
senses.titleCN: 政府监管：对行业的持续管理
senses.definition: the continuing supervision of an industry or activity by public authorities
senses.definitionCN: 公共机关对某一行业或活动的持续监督
senses.example: Banking regulation grew stricter after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后，银行业监管变得更严格。
senses.why: The noun shifts from a single rule to the whole activity of ruling: issuing, monitoring and enforcing rules.
senses.whyCN: 名词从「一条规则」转向「治理活动整体」：制定、监督与执行规则。

senses.title: Biological regulation
senses.titleCN: 生物调节：身体维持内环境稳定
senses.definition: in biology, the processes by which an organism keeps internal conditions within a workable range
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中生物把内部状态维持在可运作范围内的过程
senses.example: Body temperature regulation depends on sweating and blood flow.
senses.exampleCN: 体温调节依赖出汗与血流。
senses.why: Life uses the same controlling image: feedback loops keep a variable near a set point, just as a governor keeps a wheel steady.
senses.whyCN: 生命沿用同一个控制意象：反馈环路把某个变量维持在设定点附近，如同调速器让轮子稳定。

senses.title: Gene regulation
senses.titleCN: 基因调控：决定哪个基因何时开启
senses.definition: in molecular biology, the control of when and how strongly a gene is expressed
senses.definitionCN: 分子生物学中控制基因何时表达以及表达强弱的机制
senses.example: Gene regulation explains why two cells with the same DNA behave differently.
senses.exampleCN: 基因调控解释了为何 DNA 相同的两个细胞行为不同。
senses.why: The controlling image narrows to molecular switches: binding sites decide whether the machinery can read a gene.
senses.whyCN: 控制意象收窄到分子开关：结合位点决定读取基因的机器能否开工。

senses.title: Emotional regulation
senses.titleCN: 情绪调节：管理自己的情绪反应
senses.definition: in psychology, the ability to monitor and adjust one's emotional responses
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中监控并调整自身情绪反应的能力
senses.example: Children learn emotional regulation by naming what they feel.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童通过给感受命名来学习情绪调节。
senses.why: Psychology borrows the control metaphor for the inner state: a feeling is treated as a variable that can be adjusted rather than merely suffered.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把控制隐喻用于内在状态：情绪被当作可调变量，而不只是被动承受之物。

senses.title: Technical control
senses.titleCN: 技术调节：让设备保持在设定值
senses.definition: the automatic or manual adjustment of a machine, flow or temperature to keep it at a set level
senses.definitionCN: 自动或手动调整机器、流量或温度，使其保持在设定水平
senses.example: The valve provides fine regulation of the water flow.
senses.exampleCN: 该阀门对水流进行精细调节。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense: a device measures the deviation and corrects it, keeping the process regular.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项最字面：装置测量偏差并加以纠正，使过程保持「有规律」。

senses.title: Rules of a sport
senses.titleCN: 体育规则：比赛所依的规约
senses.definition: the official rules of a sport, or the standard period of play before extra time
senses.definitionCN: 体育项目的正式规则，或加时赛之前的常规比赛时段
senses.example: The match ended in regulation time, so no extra period was needed.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛在常规时间内结束，因此无需加时。
senses.why: Sports borrowed the legal noun: the game is governed by rules, and the unextended match is played within them.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律名词：比赛由规则治理，未加时的比赛就是在规则时段内完成的。

senses.title: An EU legal instrument
senses.titleCN: 欧盟条例：直接适用于成员国的立法形式
senses.definition: in European Union law, a binding legislative act that applies directly in all member states
senses.definitionCN: 欧盟法中直接适用于所有成员国的有约束力立法行为
senses.example: The regulation took effect in every member state on the same day.
senses.exampleCN: 该条例同一天在所有成员国生效。
senses.why: Legal systems distinguish kinds of instrument, and the EU gives the general word regulation a precise status: binding, general and directly applicable.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系区分不同立法工具，欧盟给一般词 regulation 一个精确地位：有约束力、普遍适用且直接生效。

intro.en: Regulation comes from Latin regulatio, the noun of action from regulare 'to rule, direct', built on regula 'rule, straight stick'. The English word covers both a rule and the act of keeping something steady.
intro.cn: regulation 出自拉丁 regulatio，即 regulare「管理、引导」的动作名词，而 regulare 基于 regula「规则、直木条」。英语词同时涵盖「规则」与「使某物保持稳定」的动作。

items.en: Regula meant a rule or a straight piece of wood used to check a line. It is generally linked to regere 'to rule, guide straight', though the exact derivational path is uncertain.
items.cn: regula 指规则，也指用来校验直线的直木条。它一般认为与 regere「统治、引直」相关，但确切的派生路径存疑。

items.en: The verb regulare meant 'to direct by rule, to regulate'. Classical writers used it for controlling conduct and, later, for adjusting instruments.
items.cn: 动词 regulare 意为「按规则引导、调节」。古典作者用它指控制行为，后来也用于调整器械。

items.en: Late Latin regulatio named the act of regulating. The noun passed into French and then English with the sense of rule-governed order.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 regulatio 指「调节、管理」的动作。该名词经法语进入英语，带有「依规则而形成的秩序」之义。

items.en: By the seventeenth century regulation commonly meant an authoritative rule, especially in military and administrative contexts.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，regulation 常指权威性规则，尤见于军事与行政语境。

items.en: Engineering and biology kept the older active sense: a governor or feedback loop regulates speed, temperature or gene expression.
items.cn: 工程与生物学保留了较早的主动义：调速器或反馈环路调节速度、温度或基因表达。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the link between regula and regere is generally accepted rather than fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（派生路径）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；regula 与 regere 的联系属于「一般认为是」，并非完全有文献可证。

note.en: The first group separates the regulate family; the second gives near-synonyms for rules and for control.
note.cn: 第一组区分 regulate 词族；第二组给出关于规则与控制的近义词。

entries.definition: To control or adjust. Regulation is the rule or the act as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指控制或调节；regulation 是规则或作为名词的动作。

entries.definition: An official agency or a mechanical device that regulates. It is the doer, not the rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指监管机构或调节装置；是施动者，不是规则。

entries.definition: Describing what relates to regulation. It modifies nouns such as agency or framework.
entries.definitionCN: 形容与监管相关，修饰 agency、framework 等名词。

entries.definition: The imposition of strict, often military-style order. It carries a negative tone that regulation need not have.
entries.definitionCN: 指强加严格、常为军事化的秩序，带贬义，而 regulation 未必有贬义。

entries.definition: A stated instruction about what may or must be done. A regulation is usually official and backed by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于可为或必为的明确指示；regulation 通常由官方制定并有权威支撑。

entries.definition: A formal statute enacted by a legislature. A regulation is often made under a law by an agency.
entries.definitionCN: 指立法机关通过的正式法律；regulation 常由行政机关依法制定。

entries.definition: The exercise of power to direct behaviour or a process. It is broader and does not imply written rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指引导行为或过程的权力运用，范围更广，不暗示成文规则。

entries.definition: Oversight by someone with authority. It stresses monitoring rather than issuing rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指有权威者的监督，强调监视而非制定规则。

entries.definition: A small change made to fit a condition. It matches the technical sense but lacks the sense of sustained control.
entries.definitionCN: 指为适应情况所做的小改动；与技术义相合，但缺少持续控制之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: regula 'straight stick' + -ation: keeping behaviour on a straight line.
normal.cn: regula「直木条」+ -ation：让行为保持在直线上。

normal.en: The family runs regulate, regulator, regulatory, deregulation, rule.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 regulate、regulator、regulatory、deregulation、rule。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: government regulation, gene regulation, emotional regulation, regulation time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：政府监管、基因调控、情绪调节、常规比赛时间。

normal.en: In biology, feedback keeps a variable near a set point, exactly like a governor.
normal.cn: 生物学中，反馈让变量保持在设定点附近，正如调速器。

normal.en: In EU law, a regulation is binding and directly applicable, unlike a directive.
normal.cn: 欧盟法中，条例有约束力并直接适用，与指令不同。

abstract.en: Picture a governor spinning on top of an engine, opening and closing as speed changes.
abstract.cn: 想象调速器在发动机上方旋转，随速度变化开合。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid along a drawn line to check that it has not bent.
abstract.cn: 想象一把直尺贴着画好的线，检查它是否弯曲。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat nudging a needle back to the marked number.
abstract.cn: 想象恒温器把指针推回标定的数字。

examples.en: The agency issued a regulation on aircraft noise at night.
examples.cn: 该机构发布了关于夜间飞机噪声的规章。

examples.en: Gene regulation decides which proteins a cell makes and when.
examples.cn: 基因调控决定细胞制造哪些蛋白质以及何时制造。

examples.en: The governor provides regulation of engine speed under load.
examples.cn: 调速器在负荷下调节发动机转速。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「regular（有规律的）+ tion」——让一切按规矩来 → regulation 规章、调节

root: 拉丁 regula「规则、直木条」→ regulare「按规则管理、调节」→ regulatio；英语 regulation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one motion: measure, correct, hold steady. A rule holds people steady; a governor holds a machine steady; feedback holds a body or a cell steady.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个动作：测量、纠正、保持稳定。规则让人守稳，调速器让机器稳，反馈让身体或细胞稳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a governor spinning above an engine and holding the wheel steady.
core.cn: 核心意象：调速器在发动机上方旋转，让轮子保持稳定。

branches.en: RULE AND OVERSIGHT: a single binding rule, then the whole activity of governing an industry.
branches.cn: 规则与监管：一条有约束力的规则，进而治理整个行业的活动。

branches.en: LIFE: feedback loops hold temperature and other variables near a set point.
branches.cn: 生命：反馈环路让体温等变量保持在设定点附近。

branches.en: GENES: expression is switched on, off, or turned up.
branches.cn: 基因：表达被开启、关闭或调高。

branches.en: INNER STATE: a feeling becomes something that can be monitored and adjusted.
branches.cn: 内在状态：情绪变成可被监控与调整的对象。

branches.en: MACHINES AND LAW: valves, match clocks and EU instruments each fix a standard form.
branches.cn: 机器与法律：阀门、比赛计时与欧盟条例各自固定一种标准形式。

intro.en: Regulation is a Latin noun of action in -tio on regulare, whose base regula also gives English rule and regular.
intro.cn: regulation 是加在 regulare 上的拉丁 -tio 动作名词，其词基 regula 也衍生出英语 rule 与 regular。

latinIntro.en: The regula family includes rule, regular, regulate, regulator, regulatory, regime, regiment and region, all turning on the idea of a straight line or a system of order.
latinIntro.cn: regula 词族包括 rule、regular、regulate、regulator、regulatory、regime、regiment、region，核心都围绕直线或秩序体系。

items.meaning: a ruling; the act of keeping steady
items.meaningCN: 规则；使保持稳定的动作
items.example: The regulation covers all large emitters.
items.exampleCN: 该规章覆盖所有大型排放者。

items.meaning: to control by rule or adjust
items.example: The body regulates its own temperature.

items.meaning: one who or that which regulates
items.exampleCN: 监管机构对公司处以罚款。

items.example: The train runs on a regular schedule.
items.exampleCN: 火车按固定时刻表运行。

items.example: The first rule is to sign in.
Deregulation lowered prices but raised risks.
items.exampleCN: 放松管制降低了价格，却提高了风险。

items.meaning: a system of rule or a regimen
items.example: The new regime tightened border checks.
items.exampleCN: 新政权加强了边境检查。

definition_zh: 补偿；赔偿金；报酬；弥补
definition_en: money paid to someone for loss or injury, or something that balances a disadvantage
core_image: 天平一端缺了砝码，另一端补上同等重量
scene: 工地摔伤之后，公司按合同支付了一笔款项。 The worker received compensation for his injury.
sceneCN: 这里 compensation 指「赔偿金」（第 1 个义项：为损失支付的补偿）；句意是这名工人因受伤得到了赔偿。

senses.title: Payment for loss
senses.definition: money paid to someone because they have suffered loss or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因遭受损失或伤害而支付给某人的钱
senses.example: The family received compensation for the damaged house.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人因房屋受损获得了赔偿。
senses.why: When loss cannot be undone, money is offered to make the balance level again.
senses.whyCN: 损失无法挽回时，用钱把天平重新找平。

senses.title: Pay for work
senses.definition: the money and benefits paid for a job
senses.definitionCN: 为一份工作支付的金钱与福利
senses.example: The job offers good compensation and free meals.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作报酬不错，还管饭。
senses.why: Work is also a cost to the worker, so pay is framed as making it even.
senses.whyCN: 工作对劳动者也是付出，因此工资被说成把账找平。

senses.title: Something that balances a flaw
senses.definition: something good that balances a disadvantage
senses.definitionCN: 用来抵消缺点的好处
senses.example: The quiet garden is compensation for the small rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园弥补了房间狭小。
senses.why: Not all debts are paid in money; a good point can answer a bad one.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有亏欠都用钱偿还，一个优点也能抵消一个缺点。

intro.en: Compensation comes from Latin compensare, to weigh one thing against another until they balance.
intro.cn: compensation 来自拉丁语 compensare，意为把一物与另一物相称，直到两边平衡。

items.en: Pensare meant to weigh or to pay out.
items.cn: pensare 意为称重或称量支付。

items.en: Compensare meant to balance one sum against another.
items.cn: compensare 意为用一笔抵另一笔，使两边相平。

items.en: Compensatio named the settling of that balance.
items.cn: compensatio 指把这笔账找平。

items.en: Old French compensation kept the bookkeeping sense.
items.cn: 古法语 compensation 保留了记账式的含义。

items.en: English compensation widened to injury, pay and any offset.
items.cn: 英语 compensation 扩展到伤害赔偿、薪酬与任何抵消。

note.en: The look-alike group holds related but different -tion nouns, and the meaning group separates repayment, damages and salary.
note.cn: 形近组收的是相关却不同的名词，近义组分辨偿还款项、损害赔偿金与薪水。

entries.definition: to pay someone for a loss
entries.definitionCN: 补偿；赔偿

entries.definition: a contest or a rivalry
entries.definitionCN: 竞争；比赛

entries.definition: the way parts are put together
entries.definitionCN: 构成；作文

entries.definition: money paid back to someone
entries.definitionCN: 偿还款项

entries.definition: money a court orders for harm done
entries.definitionCN: 损害赔偿金

entries.definition: fixed pay for a job
entries.definitionCN: 薪水

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a short weight on one pan, then move to pay for work and to a good point that answers a bad one.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一端缺了砝码开始，再走到工作的报酬以及用一个优点抵消一个缺点。

normal.en: Com- is together and pens means weigh, so compensation is the weight added to level the pans.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pens 是称重，compensation 就是补上去把那两盘称平的重量。

normal.en: Compensate is the verb and compensation the noun of the same settling.
normal.cn: compensate 是动词，compensation 是同一次找平的名词。

normal.en: You claim compensation, and a firm pays it.
normal.cn: 你提出索赔，公司支付赔偿。

normal.en: A compensation package is pay plus holidays plus insurance.
normal.cn: 薪酬方案是工资加假期再加保险。

normal.en: The view from the top floor is compensation for the stairs.
normal.cn: 顶楼的风景，是对爬楼梯的弥补。

abstract.en: Picture one pan of a balance rising, then a hand adding weight.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一端翘起，一只手往上加砝码。

abstract.en: Picture a pay slip folded inside a white envelope.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工资条折好放在白信封里。

abstract.en: Picture a small balcony that makes a tiny flat worth living in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小阳台，让一间小公寓值得住下去。

examples.en: She asked for compensation after the delay.
examples.cn: 延误之后她要求赔偿。

examples.en: The company paid compensation to the farmers.
examples.cn: 公司向农民支付了赔偿。

examples.en: Working from home is some compensation for the long hours.
examples.cn: 在家办公算是对长时间工作的一种弥补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compensation 记成 com（一起）加 pens（称重）加 ation：把两边的重量称平，就是补偿。

root: 源自拉丁语 compensare，com- 表示一起，pensare 表示称重，本义是把两边称平，后引申为赔偿金、报酬与弥补。

sensesIntro.en: From money that levels a loss, to pay for work, and finally to any good point that answers a bad one.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把损失称平的赔偿，到工作的报酬，最后到任何抵消缺点的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pan of a balance is short of weight, so a matching weight is added.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一端缺了砝码，另一端补上同等重量。

branches.en: Money for injury is the clearest modern sense.
branches.cn: 为伤害付钱是现代最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Pay treats work as a cost that must be made even.
branches.cn: 工资把劳动看作一份需要找平的付出。

branches.en: Not every debt is money, yet every debt wants balance.
branches.cn: 并非每笔亏欠都是钱，但每笔亏欠都想要平衡。

branches.en: Both are settled on the same old balance.
branches.cn: 两者都在同一台古老的天平上了结。

branches.en: A good point and a sum of money both answer a loss.
branches.cn: 一个优点与一笔钱，都在回应一份损失。

intro.en: Compensation joins the verb compensate with the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: compensation 由动词 compensate 加名词后缀 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pensare, to weigh, also gives us pensive and pension.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pensare（称重）还给出了 pensive 与 pension 这样的词。

items.example: The small compensations made the job bearable.
items.exampleCN: 那些小小的补偿让这份工作还过得去。

items.meaning: to make up for a loss
items.example: Nothing can compensate for the lost time.
items.exampleCN: 什么也弥补不了失去的时间。

items.example: Good coffee compensates for a poor view.
items.exampleCN: 好咖啡弥补了视野不佳。
工人们得到了全额补偿。

items.example: He worked late as a compensating effort.

items.exampleCN: 法院判给了补偿性款项。

items.meaning: a person or device that compensates
items.example: The device acts as a heat compensator.
items.exampleCN: 这个装置起热补偿作用。

items.example: The loss is compensable under the law.
items.exampleCN: 这种损失依法可获补偿。

definition_zh: 版权；著作权；取得版权；受版权保护的
definition_en: the legal right to control copies of a work, or to protect a work in this way
core_image: 书页背面一枚小小的符号，圈住了作者的名字
scene: 她把乐谱寄给出版社之前，先去登记了权利。 The composer copyrighted the song before it was played.
sceneCN: 这里 copyright 指「取得版权」（第 2 个义项：为作品办理版权保护）；句意是作曲家在歌曲演奏之前先取得了它的版权。

senses.title: The legal right over a work
senses.definition: the exclusive legal right to publish and copy a work
senses.definitionCN: 出版与复制某作品所专有的法律权利
senses.example: The copyright belongs to the author.
senses.exampleCN: 版权归作者所有。
senses.why: A made thing needs a fence, or others will carry it away.
senses.whyCN: 做出来的东西需要一道篱笆，否则会被别人搬走。

senses.title: To secure that right
senses.definition: to register or claim the legal right over a work
senses.definitionCN: 为作品登记或主张法律上的专有权
senses.example: They copyrighted the design last year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年为这项设计取得了版权。
senses.why: A right is not a wall until someone writes it down.
senses.whyCN: 权利在被人写下来之前，还算不上一道墙。

senses.title: Protected by that right
senses.definition: covered by the legal right that forbids copying
senses.definitionCN: 处于禁止他人复制的法律权利之下
senses.example: The image is copyright material.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图片是受版权保护的材料。
senses.why: The word turns from a thing owned into a fence standing around it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一件被拥有的东西，变成围着它的一道篱笆。

intro.en: Copyright joins copy, from Latin copia, plenty, with right, from Old English riht, a just claim.
intro.cn: copyright 由 copy（源自拉丁语 copia，丰富）与 right（源自古英语 riht，正当要求）合成。

items.en: Copia meant plenty, and later a transcript of a text.
items.cn: copia 意为丰富，后来指文本的抄本。

items.en: Riht meant what is just, lawful or due to a person.
items.cn: riht 意为公正的、合法的、某人应得的。

items.en: Copy named a written transcript, and right named a claim.
items.cn: copy 指书面抄本，right 指一项主张。

items.en: A printing law gave authors a limited right over their copies.
items.cn: 一部印刷法赋予作者对其印本的有限权利。

items.en: Copyright spread worldwide as printing and publishing grew.
items.cn: 随着印刷与出版发展，copyright 传遍世界。

items.en: It now covers songs, films, software and images.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖歌曲、电影、软件与图像。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the copy base, and the meaning group names other legal rights over ideas and works.
note.cn: 形近组共享 copy 词基，近义组列出其他关于作品与创意的法律权利。

entries.definition: a duplicate of an original work
entries.definitionCN: 原作品的一份复制品

entries.definition: a machine that makes copies
entries.definitionCN: 制作副本的机器

entries.definition: a person who copies documents
entries.definitionCN: 抄写文件的人

entries.definition: the right to be the only maker of an invention
entries.definitionCN: 独享某项发明制造权的权利

entries.definition: a sign that identifies a product legally
entries.definitionCN: 合法标识某产品的标志

entries.definition: a payment made for each copy sold
entries.definitionCN: 每售出一份所付的酬金

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a maker fencing a work, then move to the act of registering and to a fence already standing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从创作者为作品围起篱笆开始，再到登记这道篱笆，最后到已经立好的篱笆。

normal.en: Copyright is simply copy plus right: the right over copies.
normal.cn: copyright 就是 copy 加 right：对副本的权利。

normal.en: The symbol on a book is a small fence around the words.
normal.cn: 书上的那个符号，是围住文字的一道小篱笆。

normal.en: A song can be copied in a second, so the right must be written down.
normal.cn: 一首歌一秒就能被复制，所以这项权利必须写下来。

normal.en: Compare it with patent: one protects a work, the other an invention.
normal.cn: 和 patent 比一比：一个保护作品，一个保护发明。

normal.en: The verb is young, and it means to put that fence in place.
normal.cn: 动词用法出现较晚，意思是把这道篱笆立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a small fence around a single printed page.
abstract.cn: 想象一道小篱笆围着一页印好的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a name written at the foot of a song.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌的末尾写着一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a key that locks a box of copies.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙锁住一箱副本。

examples.en: The publisher owns the copyright to the novel.
examples.cn: 出版社拥有这部小说的版权。

examples.en: They copyrighted the software in three countries.
examples.cn: 他们在三个国家为这款软件取得了版权。

examples.en: You may not post copyright material without permission.
examples.cn: 未经许可，你不得发布受版权保护的材料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 copyright 记成 copy（复制）加 right（权利）：决定谁能复制的权利，就是版权。

root: 由 copy（源自拉丁语 copia，抄本）与 right（古英语 riht，正当权利）合成，十八世纪印刷法促成其法律含义，现指著作权。

sensesIntro.en: From a maker fencing a work, to the act of raising the fence, and at last to the fence standing around the work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从创作者为作品围起篱笆，到立起篱笆的动作，最后到已经围在作品周围的篱笆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small fence around a printed page.
core.cn: 核心意象：围着印好纸页的一道小篱笆。

branches.en: A creator holds a right over every copy of the work.
branches.cn: 创作者对作品的每一份副本都握有权利。

branches.en: Registering turns an idea of ownership into a fact on paper.
branches.cn: 登记把归属的念头变成纸上的事实。

branches.en: A work already fenced is marked as protected.
branches.cn: 已经围上篱笆的作品被标明受到保护。

branches.en: The right and the act of claiming it are two stages.
branches.cn: 权利本身与主张权利的动作是两个阶段。

branches.en: Once claimed, the work stays marked as protected.
branches.cn: 一旦主张，作品就持续被标为受保护。

intro.en: Copyright is a compound of copy and right, and it takes -ed and -able in English.
intro.cn: copyright 由 copy 与 right 复合而成，在英语里可加 -ed 与 -able。

latinIntro.en: The copy half goes back to Latin copia, plenty, which also gives copious.
latinIntro.cn: copy 这一半可追溯到拉丁语 copia（丰富），它也带来了 copious。

items.meaning: the right over copies of a work
items.meaningCN: 对作品副本所享的权利

items.meaning: able to be protected by copyright

items.exampleCN: 一名抄写员做了这份抄本。

items.example: She has a right to reply.

definition_zh: 披露；揭露；公开的信息；自我表露
definition_en: the act of making something known that was private, secret or not previously public
core_image: 一张密封的文件袋被拆开封口，里面的纸摊在桌上给所有人看
scene: 会议室里，财务主管把一只封了蜡的文件袋拆开，把里面的账目摊在桌上。 In the meeting room the finance director breaks the wax seal, spreads the accounts on the table and calls it full disclosure.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 disclosure 是「披露、公开信息」（第 1、3 个义项：公开与财务披露）；句意：财务主管拆开封蜡，把账目全部摊在桌上，称为完全披露。图中可辨识物件：文件袋、封蜡、账目表、会议桌。

pos.zh: 披露；揭露；公开的信息；自我表露

derivatives.zh: 关闭；结束（同词根，义相反方向）
围住；把……装入（en- 使进入）

senses.title: Opening what was closed
senses.titleCN: 把封闭的东西打开给人看
senses.definition: the act of making known something that was previously hidden or private
senses.definitionCN: 把此前隐藏或私密的东西公开的行为
senses.example: The disclosure of the letters changed the historical record.
senses.exampleCN: 这些书信的披露改变了历史记载。
senses.why: Latin disclaudere is dis- 'apart' plus claudere 'to shut'. A disclosure is literally an un-shutting: the cover is taken off and the contents are exposed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 disclaudere 是 dis-“分开”加 claudere“关闭”。disclosure 字面就是“打开”：盖子被拿开，内容露出来。

senses.title: The fact that is revealed
senses.definition: a piece of information that has been brought to public attention
senses.definitionCN: 被带到公众注意之下的一条信息
senses.example: The report contained several shocking disclosures.
senses.exampleCN: 报告中有几项令人震惊的揭露。
senses.why: English allows process nouns to name their own results. What is disclosed becomes a disclosure, just as a finding becomes a discovery.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许过程名词指称自身的结果。被披露的内容也就成了一个 disclosure，正如 a finding 成为一个 discovery。

senses.title: Companies publishing their accounts
senses.definition: in business and law, the publication of financial and other material facts by a company
senses.definitionCN: 商业与法律中公司公布财务及其他重要事实
senses.example: Investors relied on the annual disclosure.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者依赖年度披露。
senses.why: A listed company is legally required to un-shut its books. Disclosure here is a duty, not a favour, and its scope is defined by regulators.
senses.whyCN: 上市公司被法律要求打开账本。这里的披露是一项义务，不是恩惠，其范围由监管者界定。

senses.title: Handing over documents in litigation
senses.definition: in law, the compulsory revelation of documents and evidence to the other party before trial
senses.definitionCN: 法律中审判前向对方强制揭示文件与证据
senses.example: The court ordered full disclosure of the correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令完全开示相关通信。
senses.why: A trial is unfair if one side holds closed files. Disclosure is the procedural un-shutting that lets both parties see the same record.
senses.whyCN: 如果一方握着封闭的文件，审判就不公平。disclosure 就是程序上的“打开”，让双方看到同一份记录。

senses.title: Telling others about oneself
senses.definition: in psychology, the act of revealing personal information about oneself to another person
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中向他人透露关于自己的私人信息
senses.example: Gradual self-disclosure builds trust between strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 渐进的自我表露在陌生人之间建立信任。
senses.why: The closed thing here is the self. Self-disclosure is the deliberate opening of a private interior, and its pace measures intimacy.
senses.whyCN: 这里被封闭的东西是自我。自我表露是有意打开私密的内部，其节奏衡量着亲密程度。

senses.title: Declaring a conflict of interest
senses.definition: the formal statement of a personal interest that might bias a judgement or decision
senses.definitionCN: 对可能影响判断或决定的个人利益作出正式说明
senses.example: The reviewer filed a conflict-of-interest disclosure.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人提交了利益冲突披露。
senses.why: The disclosure does not remove the conflict; it makes it visible so others can weigh the judgement. Openness substitutes for purity.
senses.whyCN: 披露并不消除利益冲突；它让冲突可见，以便他人权衡判断。公开替代了纯洁。

senses.title: Government opening its records
senses.definition: in public administration, the release of official information to citizens on request or by policy
senses.definitionCN: 公共行政中应请求或按政策向公民发布官方信息
senses.example: Freedom-of-information laws widen government disclosure.
senses.exampleCN: 信息自由法扩大了政府的信息公开。
senses.why: Here the closed drawer belongs to the state. Disclosure becomes a democratic mechanism: the public can check what was done in its name.
senses.whyCN: 这里封闭的抽屉属于国家。披露成为一种民主机制：公众可以核查以自己名义做了什么。

senses.title: Openness with no reservation
senses.definition: the state of hiding nothing relevant, especially in the phrase full disclosure
senses.definitionCN: 不隐瞒任何相关事项的状态，尤用于短语 full disclosure
senses.example: Full disclosure requires mentioning the failed trial too.
senses.exampleCN: 完全披露也要求提到那次失败的试验。
senses.why: Full disclosure is a standard rather than an act: every relevant drawer must be opened. The adjective sets the completeness, the noun the opening.
senses.whyCN: full disclosure 是一个标准而非一次动作：每个相关抽屉都必须打开。形容词规定完整度，名词规定打开。

senses.title: A formal statement that discloses
senses.definition: a document or section of a document in which required information is set out
senses.definitionCN: 载明所需信息的文件或文件中的一节
senses.example: Read the risk disclosure before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签署前请阅读风险披露声明。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the act to the paper that performs it. A disclosure statement is the institutional form of the un-shutting.
senses.whyCN: 名词从行为转向执行该行为的纸张。披露声明是“打开”这一动作的制度化形式。

intro.en: Disclosure is dis- plus close plus -ure. Close comes from Latin claudere 'to shut', through Old French clos. The verb disclose existed in English by the 14th century, and the noun followed with the French-style suffix -ure.
intro.cn: disclosure 是 dis- 加 close 再加 -ure。close 来自拉丁 claudere“关闭”，经古法语 clos 传入。动词 disclose 在 14 世纪已见于英语，名词随后以法语式后缀 -ure 构成。

items.en: Claudere meant 'to shut, to close'. Its past participle clausus supplies clause, close, cloister and the -clud- of include and exclude.
items.cn: claudere 意为“关闭”。其过去分词 clausus 给出 clause、close、cloister，以及 include、exclude 中的 -clud-。

items.en: Classical Latin had no common verb *disclaudere; the negative verb took shape in Romance. Old French built desclore from des- plus clore, and English borrowed that form. The Latin reconstruction is marked here as a reconstructed form, not an attested classical verb.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语并无常见的 *disclaudere 动词，否定形式是在罗曼语中成形的。古法语用 des- 加 clore 构成 desclore，英语借入这一形式。此处的拉丁重构仅作“重构形式”标注，并非古典拉丁语中实际可查的动词。

items.en: Old French desclore meant 'to open up, to reveal'. Its stem supplied Middle English disclosen, later disclose.
items.cn: 古法语 desclore 意为“打开、揭示”。其词干给出中古英语 disclosen，后作 disclose。

items.en: The verb appears in the 14th century with the sense 'to open up, to expose to view'. It is used of secrets, wounds and enclosed places alike.
items.cn: 动词在 14 世纪出现，意为“打开、使显露”。它既用于秘密，也用于伤口与围合之处。

items.en: The noun is formed with -ure, the same suffix as in closure and exposure. Early uses concern the act of revealing; the 'thing revealed' sense follows.
items.cn: 名词以 -ure 构成，与 closure、exposure 同后缀。早期用法指揭示行为，随后出现“被揭示之事”的义项。

items.en: Securities law in the 1930s made disclosure a technical duty. Psychology and law later added self-disclosure and pre-trial disclosure as fixed terms.
items.cn: 1930 年代的证券法使 disclosure 成为一项技术性义务。心理学与法学随后加入 self-disclosure 与审判前开示等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the container word and its opposite. The meaning group contrasts voluntary openness with leakage, revelation and announcement.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、容器类词与其反义方向；词义组把自愿公开与泄露、揭示、宣布区分开。

entries.definition: to make known or expose to view. The noun adds -ure to this verb.
entries.definitionCN: 使知晓或使显露。名词在其上加 -ure。

entries.definition: something enclosed, or the act of enclosing. It uses en- 'in' with the same claudere root, so it shuts in rather than opens out.
entries.definitionCN: 被围起之物，或围合行为。它用 en-“内”加同一 claudere 词根，因此是关进去而非打开。

entries.definition: the act of closing, or a sense of resolution. It is disclosure with the opening removed.
entries.definitionCN: 关闭行为，或一种了结感。它是去掉了“打开”的 disclosure。

entries.definition: a surprising fact made known, or divine disclosure. It stresses the impact of the news, while disclosure stresses the act and often a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 令人意外的事实被公布，或神的启示。它强调消息的冲击，而 disclosure 强调行为，常含义务。

entries.definition: the unauthorized release of information. A disclosure may be required by law; a leak never is.
entries.definitionCN: 未经授权的信息泄露。disclosure 可能是法律要求的；leak 从来不是。

entries.definition: a formal public statement. It is addressed outward to an audience, while disclosure is about removing concealment.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明。它朝外对受众说话，而 disclosure 关注的是去除掩盖。

entries.definition: the quality of operating openly. It is a standing condition, while a disclosure is a particular act.
entries.definitionCN: 公开运作的品质。它是持续状态，而 disclosure 是具体行为。

entries.definition: an admission of wrongdoing. It carries guilt, which disclosure does not necessarily carry.
entries.definitionCN: 对过错的承认。它带有罪感，而 disclosure 未必带有。

normalIntro.en: These hooks reduce the word to one physical act, un-shutting, and then locate who owns the closed thing in each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词缩成一个物理动作——打开，然后在每个义项里找出那个被关着的东西归谁。

normal.en: See dis- + close: the shut thing is un-shut.
normal.cn: 看见 dis- 加 close：被关上的东西被打开。

normal.en: Picture the wax seal breaking on the file. That crack is the disclosure.
normal.cn: 想象文件上的封蜡裂开。那道裂缝就是 disclosure。

normal.en: In finance, the drawer belongs to the company and the law says it must open.
normal.cn: 在金融里，抽屉属于公司，而法律说它必须打开。

normal.en: In psychology, the drawer is the self, and the person chooses when to open it.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，抽屉是自我，而本人选择何时打开。

normal.en: Contrast enclosure: en- shuts in, dis- lets out.
normal.cn: 对比 enclosure：en- 关进去，dis- 放出来。

abstract.en: Reduce every sense to two questions: what was closed, and who has the right to open it?
abstract.cn: 把每个义项缩成两个问题：什么被关着，谁有权打开？

abstract.en: Notice that disclosure changes relationships, not facts: the fact stays, the concealment ends.
abstract.cn: 注意披露改变的是关系而不是事实：事实不变，掩盖结束。

abstract.en: Keep the image of the seam: a disclosure is visible exactly at the line where covering meets content.
abstract.cn: 记住接缝的意象：披露恰恰在遮盖与内容相接的那条线上可见。

examples.en: The newspaper's disclosure forced the minister to resign.
examples.cn: 报纸的披露迫使部长辞职。

examples.en: Regulations require full disclosure of any conflict of interest.
examples.cn: 规定要求完全披露任何利益冲突。

examples.en: Too much self-disclosure too early can end a friendship.
examples.cn: 过早过多的自我表露可能终结一段友谊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“地斯克罗热”：地里的斯克罗（disclose）被热得裂开，封口一开就全露出来——disclosure 就是披露。

root: 拉丁语 claudere“关闭”，加 dis- 构成“打开、揭示”的动词（拉丁少见，主要由罗曼语继承），经古法语 desclore 进入中古英语作 disclosen、disclose；加名词后缀 -ure 构成 disclosure。同根词有 include、exclude、conclude、clause、cloister。

sensesIntro.en: Disclosure is one physical gesture with many owners. A file is un-shut, a company's books are un-shut, a litigant's documents are un-shut, a self is un-shut, a government's records are un-shut. The nine senses differ in what was concealed and whether opening is voluntary, required or compulsory, but all of them turn concealment into visibility.
sensesIntro.cn: disclosure 是同一个物理动作，只是被打开的东西归属不同：文件被打开、公司账本被打开、诉讼方的文件被打开、自我被打开、政府记录被打开。九个义项的区别在于被掩盖的是什么，以及打开是自愿、应要求还是强制；但它们都把掩盖变成了可见。

core.en: Un-shutting: removing a cover so that the contents can be seen.
core.cn: 打开：移开遮盖，让内容被看见。

branches.en: GENERAL: the act of revealing, and the fact revealed.
branches.cn: 一般义：揭示行为，以及被揭示的事实。

branches.en: LAW AND BUSINESS: required publication and the documents that carry it.
branches.cn: 法律与商业：强制公布，以及承载它的文件。

branches.en: PSYCHOLOGY: opening the private self to another.
branches.cn: 心理学：把私密的自我向他人打开。

branches.en: ETHICS: declaring interests and hiding nothing relevant.
branches.cn: 伦理：声明利益，不隐瞒任何相关事项。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE: the state opening its records to citizens.
branches.cn: 治理：国家向公民打开记录。

intro.en: Disclosure is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb and a French noun suffix. The items follow claudere through English and show how the same root shuts, encloses and excludes.
intro.cn: disclosure 由拉丁前缀、拉丁动词与法语名词后缀组成。下列条目追踪 claudere 在英语中的走向，展示同一词根如何关闭、围住与排除。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb of shutting and its participle. They explain why 'close', 'clause' and 'cloister' all contain the same idea of an enclosed space.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“关闭”的动词及其分词。它们解释了为什么 close、clause、cloister 都含有同一个“围合空间”的观念。

items.meaning: the act of revealing; a revealed fact
items.meaningCN: 披露行为；被披露的事实

items.meaning: to make known; to expose to view
items.example: He refused to disclose his sources.

items.meaning: the act of closing; a sense of ending
items.example: The talks reached a satisfying closure.
items.exampleCN: 会谈达成了令人满意的了结。

items.example: Please enclose a copy of the receipt.

items.exampleCN: 这些规则把兼职人员排除在外。

items.meaning: to shut in; to contain as part
to shut together; to bring to an end
a closed unit of a sentence or document
an enclosed religious walk or community
items.example: The monks walked in the cloister.

latinEntries.meaning: a shut place; a barrier, a cloister

definition_zh: 证词；证言；见证；（对某事的）明证
definition_en: a formal statement, especially one made under oath in court, that something is true
core_image: 证人站在庭上，手按誓词，把所见一句一句说给速记员
scene: 证人席上的人举起手，速记员开始敲下他说的每一句。 Her testimony lasted nearly three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 testimony 指证人在法庭上给出的证词（第 1 个义项：法庭上作出的正式陈述）；句意为她的证词持续了将近三个小时。图中可辨识物件：证人席、速记键盘、誓词卡、记者笔记本。

derivatives.zh: 遗嘱；证明（同出 testari 词根）

senses.title: Sworn statement in court
senses.definition: a formal statement made under oath by a witness in a legal proceeding
senses.definitionCN: 证人在法律程序中宣誓后作出的正式陈述
senses.example: Her testimony lasted nearly three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她的证词持续了将近三个小时。
senses.why: Testimony comes from Latin testimonium, built on testis 'witness': it is the words a witness contributes to a case.
senses.whyCN: testimony 出自拉丁 testimonium，词根是 testis「证人」：它是证人为案件提供的言辞。

senses.title: Expert evidence
senses.definition: the statement of a specialist explaining technical matters to a court
senses.definitionCN: 专家向法庭解释专门问题的陈述
senses.example: The geologist's testimony turned on the age of the layer.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家的证言关键在于那一层的年代。
senses.why: A specialist is still a witness, so the word covers informed opinion as well as eyewitness fact.
senses.whyCN: 专家同样是证人，因此这个词既指亲见的事实，也指有依据的专业判断。

senses.title: Bearing witness to something
senses.definition: a public act of confirming something one has seen or known
senses.definitionCN: 公开确认自己所见所知的行为
senses.example: Her letters bear testimony to a long friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书信见证了长久的友谊。
senses.why: The old phrase bear testimony keeps the witness in view while the object shifts from a crime to a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 「作见证」这一旧说法仍保留「见证人」的意思，只是对象从罪行换成了关系。

senses.title: A clear sign of something
senses.definition: something that serves as clear proof of a quality or an event
senses.definitionCN: 作为某品质或某事件的明确证明的事物
senses.example: The rebuilt square is testimony to the city's recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 重建的广场是该城复苏的明证。
senses.why: When an object testifies, it does what a witness does: it makes a fact publicly undeniable.
senses.whyCN: 当一件物品「作证」时，它做的事与证人相同：让某项事实变得公开而无可否认。

senses.title: Written statement
senses.definition: a written statement sworn or affirmed before a person with authority
senses.definitionCN: 在有权者面前宣誓或确认的书面陈述
senses.example: The clerk read the written testimony into the record.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员把书面证词读入案卷。
senses.why: Procedure accepts words on paper as testimony, so the noun covers documents as well as speech.
senses.whyCN: 程序法承认纸面文字同样构成证词，因此这个词也指文件。

senses.title: The voices of many witnesses
senses.definition: the collected statements of several witnesses considered together
senses.definitionCN: 把若干证人的陈述合并考察
senses.example: The testimony of the passengers contradicted the driver's account.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客们的证词与司机的说法相矛盾。
senses.why: The uncountable use treats many statements as one body of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法把许多陈述当成一整份证据。

senses.title: Public declaration of faith
senses.titleCN: 宗教集会中的信仰见证
senses.definition: a personal account of religious experience given to a congregation
senses.definitionCN: 在会众面前讲述个人宗教经历的陈述
senses.example: He gave his testimony before the congregation at the spring meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他在春季聚会上向会众讲述了自己的信仰见证。
senses.why: Religious communities borrowed the legal noun for a statement whose truth rests on the speaker's own life.
senses.whyCN: 宗教群体借用了这个法律名词，用来指以讲述者自身经历为凭的陈述。

senses.title: Statement to an inquiry
senses.titleCN: 听证会或调查中的正式陈述
senses.definition: a formal statement given to a committee, commission or investigation
senses.definitionCN: 向委员会、调查组或听证会作出的正式陈述
senses.example: Her testimony before the committee was released in full.
senses.exampleCN: 她在委员会上的证词被全文公布。
senses.why: Outside a courtroom the noun still means a formal statement on oath, which is why hearings use it.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭之外，这个词仍指正式宣誓的陈述，因此听证会沿用它。

intro.en: Testimony comes through Anglo-French from Latin testimonium 'evidence, witness', built on testis 'witness' plus the noun suffix -monium. It is recorded in English from the thirteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: testimony 经盎格鲁—法语来自拉丁 testimonium「证据、见证」，由 testis「证人」加名词后缀 -monium 构成，十三世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Testis meant 'witness'. Its deeper origin is not established; the suggestion that it began as 'third person standing by' is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: testis 意为「证人」。其更深来源未获证明；认为它原指「站在一旁的第三人」的说法属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Testis plus -monium produced testimonium 'evidence, testimony, proof'.
items.cn: testis 加 -monium 构成 testimonium「证据、证词、证明」。

items.en: Anglo-French carried the noun into English law in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—法语在十三世纪把这个名词带入英格兰的法律用语。

items.en: From the first records testimony meant the statement of a witness, given in a case and open to challenge.
items.cn: 从最早的书证起，testimony 就指证人在案件中作出、可被质疑的陈述。

items.en: In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun widened to public declarations of faith and to any clear sign of a fact.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪，这个名词扩展到公开的信仰陈述以及任何明确的事实迹象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of testis is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is uncertain. The anatomical testis is a separate homonym and no derivation from the witness word is demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：testis 在拉丁语之前的历史属于重构，英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。解剖学意义上的 testis 是另一个同形词，尚无证据显示它由「证人」这个词派生。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same testis stock that are often confused; group two holds the kinds of statement a case may rest on.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 testis 词干、常被混淆的词；第二组是一桩案件可能依据的各类陈述。

entries.definition: From testari 'to make a will', built on testis: a document declaring one's wishes after death.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 testari「立遗嘱」，词根为 testis：声明身后意愿的文件。

entries.definition: A letter testifying to a person's character or service, rather than words spoken in court.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人品行或工作经历的信件，而不是庭上说的话。

entries.definition: A legal adjective for someone who has left a valid will, from the will-making sense of testari.
entries.definitionCN: 法律形容词，指留下有效遗嘱的人，取自 testari 的立遗嘱义。

entries.definition: An anatomical word from Latin testiculus; its relation to the witness word is not demonstrated.
entries.definitionCN: 解剖学术语，出自拉丁 testiculus；它与「证人」一词的关系未获证明。

entries.definition: The broad term for anything that proves a fact, of which testimony is one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指一切能证明事实的材料，证词只是其中一类。

entries.definition: A plain account of facts; it need not be sworn or given in court.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实的平实陈述，不必宣誓，也不必须在法庭作出。

entries.definition: A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation, usually for use in legal proceedings.
entries.definitionCN: 经宣誓或确认的书面陈述，通常用于法律程序。

entries.definition: Sworn testimony recorded out of court before trial, used later as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 审前在庭外录取的宣誓证词，供日后作为证据使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Testis 'witness' plus -monium: the words a witness brings.
normal.cn: testis「证人」加 -monium：证人带来的言辞。

normal.en: The family runs testify, testimony, testifier, testimonial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 testify、testimony、testifier 与 testimonial。

normal.en: Courts say give testimony and hear testimony; reporters say sworn testimony.
normal.cn: 法庭上说「提供证词」「听取证词」，报道里说「宣誓证词」。

normal.en: The abstract use is testimony to something: testimony to her patience.
normal.cn: 抽象用法是 testimony to：对她的耐心的明证。

normal.en: The anatomical testicle is a separate homonym, not a relative proved by derivation.
normal.cn: 解剖学上的 testicle 是另一个同形词，并非已证实的同族词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised over a book before the first sentence is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象在说出第一句之前，一只手先按在书上。

abstract.en: Picture a stone plaque that keeps saying what happened long after the witnesses have gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石牌，在证人都不在了之后仍不断说明发生过什么。

abstract.en: Picture a room where many separate voices are folded into one page.
abstract.cn: 想象许多彼此独立的声音被折进同一页纸里。

examples.en: The court heard testimony from six witnesses in two days.
examples.cn: 法庭在两天内听取了六名证人的证词。

examples.en: The broken tools are testimony to how little the crew had to work with.
examples.cn: 这些破损的工具说明施工队手里的条件多么有限。

examples.en: Her testimony to the commission was published with the exhibits.
examples.cn: 她向委员会所作的证词连同证物一并公布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「test（作证）+ imony」——站在证人席上说出所见：证词、见证

root: 拉丁 testimonium「证据、见证」= testis「证人」+ -monium；testis 更深来源不确定，与解剖学同形词无已证实的派生关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one witness in place while its voice moves: a sworn statement, an expert opinion, a public act of witnessing, a sign left by events, a written page, the combined voices of many, a declaration of faith and a statement to an inquiry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一位证人留在原处，只让他的声音移动：宣誓陈述、专家意见、公开见证、事件留下的明证、书面页、众人之声的合并、信仰陈述，以及向调查组的正式陈说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a witness at the stand with one hand raised, speaking sentence by sentence to a recorder.
core.cn: 核心意象：证人站在证人席上，一只手举起，一句一句地对速记员说话。

branches.en: THE SWORN VOICE: the same stand holds an eyewitness and a specialist explaining a field.
branches.cn: 宣誓的声音：同一个证人席上，既站着目击者，也站着解释专业的专家。

branches.en: BEYOND THE COURT: a life and a rebuilt square can both testify to something without speaking.
branches.cn: 走出法庭：一段人生与一座重建的广场都能不发一言地作证。

branches.en: ON PAPER: the statement is sworn in writing and read into the record.
branches.cn: 落在纸上：陈述以书面形式宣誓，再被读入案卷。

branches.en: MANY AT ONCE: separate statements are gathered into one body of testimony.
branches.cn: 多人同时：各自独立的陈述被汇成一份证词总体。

branches.en: ELSEWHERE SPEAKING: a congregation and a commission both ask for a formal personal account.
branches.cn: 在别处陈说：会众与调查委员会都要一份正式的个人陈述。

intro.en: Testimony is a Latin noun whose root, suffix and relatives all remain readable in English.
intro.cn: testimony 是一个拉丁名词，其词根、后缀与同族词在英语中仍然可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin testis 'witness' gives testimony, testify, testament and testimonial, all through the act of calling a witness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 testis「证人」衍生 testimony、testify、testament 与 testimonial，都经由「传唤证人」这一动作。

items.example: The root names the person who speaks.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指出面说话的人。

items.example: The suffix turns the witness into the evidence produced.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「证人」转成由其产生的证据。
这家公司出具了一封证明信。

items.example: The will was read as a testament.
items.exampleCN: 这份遗嘱被当作郑重声明宣读。
两名职员证明了签名的真实性。

latinEntries.structure: testari, testatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)
latinEntries.meaning: to witness, to make a will

latinEntries.structure: testificari, testificatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_zh: 裁决；评断；结论；（陪审团或验尸官的）裁定
definition_en: the formal decision of a jury or an official inquiry, or any opinion reached after weighing the evidence
core_image: 十二个人从一间小屋里走出来，领头的人把一张折好的纸条递到书记员手里
scene: 十二个人在小屋里商议了四个小时，领头的人把写有结论的纸条交给书记员。 The foreman handed the verdict to the clerk after four hours of deliberation.
sceneCN: 这里 verdict 指「陪审团经商议后作出的正式结论」（第 1 个义项：陪审团裁决）；句意为商议四小时后，领头的人把裁决结果交给书记员。图中可辨识物件：折好的纸条、陪审席、书记员的登记册、法庭围栏。

derivatives.zh: 诚实的；真实的（同出「真」的词根）
真实；真理（同出「真」的词根）
格言；正式陈述（同出「说」的词根）

senses.title: A jury's decision
senses.definition: the formal finding of a jury on whether the accused is guilty or not guilty
senses.definitionCN: 陪审团就被指控者有罪与否作出的正式结论
senses.example: The foreman handed the verdict to the clerk after four hours of deliberation.
senses.exampleCN: 商议四小时后，领头的人把裁决结果交给书记员。
senses.why: Verdict is vere 'truly' plus dictum 'saying': the word originally meant a true statement, and the jury's function is to say what it holds to be true about the facts.
senses.whyCN: verdict 是 vere「真实地」加 dictum「陈述」：这个词原意是一句真话，而陪审团的职能正是说出它对事实所认定的真相。

senses.title: A finding of an inquiry
senses.titleCN: 调查或验尸得出的结论
senses.definition: the conclusion recorded by an official inquiry, such as a coroner's finding on a death
senses.definitionCN: 官方调查所记录的结论，如验尸官对死因的认定
senses.example: The coroner returned a verdict of accidental death.
senses.exampleCN: 验尸官作出意外死亡的裁定。
senses.why: An inquiry speaks in the same voice as a jury: it states what it finds to be true, so the noun serves both without strain.
senses.whyCN: 调查与陪审团以同一种口吻发言：它陈述自己认定的事实，因此这个名词无需费力就能适用于两者。

senses.title: A considered opinion
senses.definition: any judgement reached after weighing evidence, even where no court is involved
senses.definitionCN: 经权衡证据后作出判断，即使不涉及法院
senses.example: Our verdict, after three months of testing, is that the material is sound.
senses.exampleCN: 经过三个月测试，我们的结论是这种材料可靠。
senses.why: Once a verdict is simply a true saying, it can be pronounced by anyone who has done the weighing, not only by twelve sworn citizens.
senses.whyCN: 既然裁决不过是一句真实的话，任何做过权衡的人都可以作出，而不必是十二名宣誓的公民。

senses.title: The public's judgement
senses.titleCN: 公众或媒体对人的评价
senses.definition: the opinion formed about a person, product or event by the public at large
senses.definitionCN: 公众对某人、某产品或某事件形成的看法
senses.example: The verdict on the new bridge was favourable long before it opened.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新桥远在通车之前就已获得好评。
senses.why: The metaphor puts the public in the jury box: collective opinion borrows the finality of a court's word.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把公众放进陪审席：集体意见借用了法庭话语的终局性。

senses.title: An official review decision in sport
senses.titleCN: 体育复核后的官方判定
senses.definition: a final decision by a reviewing official or video panel on what happened in play
senses.definitionCN: 复核官员或视频裁判组对场上事实作出的最终判定
senses.example: The video panel's verdict overturned the goal within thirty seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 视频裁判组在三十秒内推翻了进球判定。
senses.why: Sport has added review panels that pronounce on facts, and they borrow the word because their finding must end the argument.
senses.whyCN: 体育增设了对事实作出宣告的复核小组，它们借用了这个词，因为其结论必须终结争论。

senses.title: A decision on a submitted work
senses.titleCN: 对提交作品的最终评定
senses.definition: the final decision of a panel on an entry or application
senses.definitionCN: 评审团对参赛作品或申请作出的最终决定
senses.example: The jury's verdict placed the design second in its category.
senses.exampleCN: 评审团的评定把该设计排在其类别第二。
senses.why: A competition needs a pronouncement that ends the comparison, and the courtroom noun supplies the finality.
senses.whyCN: 比赛需要一个终结比较的宣告，而法庭名词正好提供这种终局性。

senses.title: The outcome of a test or comparison
senses.titleCN: 测试或比较得出的结局性结论
senses.definition: the conclusion produced by a test, comparison or long observation
senses.definitionCN: 测试、比较或长期观察所得出的结论
senses.example: Field trials gave a clear verdict: the treated plots held water longer.
senses.exampleCN: 田间试验给出明确结论：处理过的地块保水更久。
senses.why: The noun is used for anything that finally settles a question, because settling is what the original word meant.
senses.whyCN: 凡能最终了结一个问题的事物都用这个名词，因为「了结」正是原词之义。

senses.title: A verdict read as a sentence
senses.titleCN: 裁决作为判词/量刑依据
senses.definition: the formal answer of guilty or not guilty, on which sentence then follows
senses.definitionCN: 有罪或无罪的形式回答，随后据以量刑
senses.example: The verdict was not guilty, and the court had nothing left to impose.
senses.exampleCN: 裁决为无罪，法院也就无从量刑。
senses.why: English keeps verdict for the answer and sentence for the consequence, a division that legal usage has held for centuries.
senses.whyCN: 英语用 verdict 指回答，用 sentence 指后果，这一区分法律用法已维持数百年。

intro.en: Verdict comes through Anglo-French verdit from Latin veredictum, built on vere 'truly' plus dictum 'saying'. The word meant a true statement before it meant a jury's answer.
intro.cn: verdict 经英属法语 verdit 来自拉丁 veredictum，由 vere「真实地」加 dictum「陈述」构成。这个词先指真实的陈述，后指陪审团的回答。

items.en: Verus meant true, and its adverb vere meant truly; the same root gives veritas and the English verity.
items.cn: verus 意为真的，其副词 vere 意为真实地；同一词根还给 veritas 与英语 verity。

items.en: Dictum was a thing said, from dicere 'to say'; in legal Latin it named a formal statement rather than casual speech.
items.cn: dictum 是所说的话，出自 dicere「说」；在法律拉丁中它指正式陈述，而非随意言谈。

items.en: Veredictum meant a true declaration; the compound is usually read as 'truly said', though the exact force of the first element is a matter of interpretation.
items.cn: veredictum 意为真实的宣告；这个复合词通常被理解为「真实地说出」，不过第一个成分的确切作用属解释问题。

items.en: Anglo-French verdit narrowed the word to the answer a jury gives, which is how English received it in the medieval period.
items.cn: 英属法语 verdit 把这个词收窄为陪审团给出的回答，英语在中世纪正是这样接收它的。

items.en: By the early modern period verdict was fixed to the jury's finding, with ruling and judgment covering the court's own decisions.
items.cn: 到近代早期，verdict 已固定为陪审团的认定，而法院自己的决定由 ruling 与 judgment 承担。

items.en: The first English date is approximate: medieval use is recorded, but the earliest citation in English texts is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 英语首见年代为约数：中世纪用例已有记录，但英语文本中的最早书证没有精确年代。

note.en: The first group shares the 'saying' stem or looks close to it; the second group names decisions that are often mistaken for a verdict.
note.cn: 第一组共享「说」这一词干或形近；第二组是常被误当作裁决的其他决定。

entries.definition: A formal saying or pronouncement, from the same dictum; it carries no decision and binds nobody.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的说法或宣告，同出 dictum；它不含决定，也不约束任何人。

entries.definition: To say beforehand, from dicere; it is about the future and needs no evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 预先说出，出自 dicere；它关于未来，不需要证据。

entries.definition: To check that something is true, from verus; it tests a claim rather than settling it.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否真实，出自 verus；它检验说法，而非了结它。

entries.definition: Truth or a true statement, from verus; an abstract noun with no courtroom role.
entries.definitionCN: 真理或真实的陈述，出自 verus；抽象名词，无法庭职能。

entries.definition: From ius 'right', not verus; it names fairness, not a finding.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 ius「权利」而非 verus；命名公平，而非认定。

entries.definition: The court's decision on law or procedure; it answers the judge's question, while verdict answers the jury's.
entries.definitionCN: 法院就法律或程序作出的决定；它回答法官的问题，而 verdict 回答陪审团的问题。

entries.definition: The full decision including reasons and order; verdict is only the answer to the charge.
entries.definitionCN: 包含理由与命令的完整决定；verdict 只是对被控罪名的回答。

entries.definition: The penalty imposed after a verdict; it is the consequence, never the finding.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决之后所施加的处罚；它是后果，绝不是认定。

entries.definition: The conclusion of an investigation or tribunal, which may or may not be phrased as a verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 调查或裁判所的结论，可能以裁决的措辞表达，也可能不。

entries.definition: Any settled choice, from a court or from a committee; it lacks the jury flavour of verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 任何已定的选择，可出自法院或委员会；它不带陪审团色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin true and saying, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「真」与「陈述」、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Vere is 'truly' and dictum is 'saying', so a verdict is a true saying, the sentence that settles what the facts are.
normal.cn: vere 是「真实地」，dictum 是「陈述」，所以裁决就是一句真话，一句了结事实的话。

normal.en: The family runs verdict, dictum, predict, verify, verity and veracious.
normal.cn: 同族词有 verdict、dictum、predict、verify、verity 与 veracious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the courtroom sense: reach a verdict, a guilty verdict, return a verdict.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法庭义：作出裁决、有罪裁决、宣布裁决。

normal.en: A verdict is the answer, a sentence is the consequence; English has kept them apart for centuries.
normal.cn: 裁决是回答，量刑是后果；英语数百年来把两者分开。

normal.en: Anyone who has weighed the evidence can issue a verdict, which is why the word escaped the courtroom.
normal.cn: 任何权衡过证据的人都能作出裁决，这个词正是因此走出了法庭。

abstract.en: Picture a folded slip of paper passed through a hatch before anyone speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折好的纸条在所有人开口之前从窗口递出。

abstract.en: Picture twelve chairs pushed back at once, and the corridor filling with waiting people.
abstract.cn: 想象十二把椅子同时被推开，走廊里立刻挤满等候的人。

abstract.en: Picture a set of scales coming to rest, and the room deciding to believe the pointer.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平静止下来，屋子里的人都决定相信那根指针。

examples.en: The jury reached its verdict after two days.
examples.cn: 陪审团在两天后作出了裁决。

examples.en: Historians have not yet delivered a verdict on that treaty.
examples.cn: 历史学者尚未对那项条约给出定论。

examples.en: The inquest recorded an open verdict because the cause was unclear.
examples.cn: 因死因不明，验尸庭记录了存疑裁决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ver（真）+ dict（说）」——一句被认定为真的话 → 裁决

root: 拉丁 verus「真」的副词 vere「真实地」+ dictum「陈述」（出自 dicere「说」）→ veredictum「真实宣告」→ 英属法语 verdit → 英语 verdict。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one slip of paper: a jury writes it, an inquiry copies it, anyone who has weighed evidence can pronounce it, the public adopts it, a video panel borrows it, a competition uses it, a field trial produces it, and a court then decides what follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一张纸条：陪审团写下它，调查照抄它，任何权衡过证据的人都能说出它，公众采纳它，视频裁判组借用它，比赛使用它，田间试验产出它，最后由法院决定接下来怎么办。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded slip handed through a hatch before anyone in the room speaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张折好的纸条在屋里所有人开口之前从窗口递出。

branches.en: TWO OFFICIAL VOICES: a jury and an inquiry both state what they find to be true.
branches.cn: 两种官方声音：陪审团与调查都在陈述它们认定的真相。

branches.en: FROM COURT TO PUBLIC: once it is simply a true saying, the public can speak it too.
branches.cn: 从法庭到公众：既然它只是一句真话，公众也能说。

branches.en: PANELS OF TWO KINDS: sport and competitions borrow the word because their finding must end the argument.
branches.cn: 两种评审团：体育与比赛借用这个词，因为其结论必须终结争论。

branches.en: THE TEST SPEAKS: a field trial can deliver a verdict, since settling a question is the original sense.
branches.cn: 试验发言：田间试验也能给出裁决，因为「了结问题」正是原义。

branches.en: THE ANSWER AND THE PRICE: the verdict answers the charge, and sentence pays for it.
branches.cn: 回答与代价：裁决回答指控，量刑为其付出代价。

intro.en: Verdict is two Latin words fused: an adverb of truth and a noun of saying. Both halves are productive elsewhere in English.
intro.cn: verdict 是两个拉丁词融合而成：一个表真的副词与一个表陈述的名词，两半在英语别处都有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Latin verus gives verify, verity and veracious; dicere gives dictum, predict and contradict; the fusion gives verdict alone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 verus 给出 verify、verity 与 veracious；dicere 给出 dictum、predict 与 contradict；融合形式只给出 verdict。

items.example: The form used inside the compound.
It builds verify, to make true or check.
The truth half on its own.
The saying half on its own.
It builds predict, to say beforehand.

definition_zh: 判断力；看法；判决；天谴
definition_en: the ability to form sound opinions, an opinion so formed, or a formal ruling by a court
core_image: 天平上的砝码落下，指针抖了一下，停住
scene: 评审室里，三位评委听完演奏，各自在纸上写下分数。 Her judgment of the young pianist was kinder than the others'.
sceneCN: 这里 judgment 指「经思考形成的评价」（第 1 个义项：形成稳妥看法的能力及其结果）；句意为她对那位年轻钢琴家的评价比其他人宽厚。场景要素：评分纸、铅笔、舞台监听音箱。

derivatives.zh: 与 judgment 同出拉丁语中「法官」一词，指审理者或审理这一行为
由拉丁语「法庭的」一词进入英语，指与司法有关的
由 judge 加形容词后缀构成，指有见地的、审慎的
由 judgmental 加副词后缀构成，指以评判的姿态；属另一条形容词线
由表「在前」的前缀加「判断」的拉丁词构成，指预先形成的判断，后指偏见

senses.title: The ability to form sound opinions
senses.definition: the capacity to weigh evidence and reach a sensible conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 权衡证据并得出合宜结论的能力
senses.example: Years of editing gave her a reliable judgment about which submissions would sell.
senses.exampleCN: 多年编辑经验让她对哪些投稿卖得动有可靠的判断。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it joins law and speaking, so judging originally meant declaring what is right, and the mental capacity sense grew from that authority.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁词把法律与言说连在一起，因此「判断」原指宣示何为正当，心智能力义由此权威感生长出来。

senses.title: An opinion reached
senses.definition: a conclusion one has come to about a person, work or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对人、作品或情形得出的结论
senses.example: My judgment is that the proposal is sound but the timing is wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 我的看法是方案本身可靠，但时机不对。
senses.why: Once the capacity produces something, the same noun names the product, which is why it appears with possessives.
senses.whyCN: 能力一旦产出结果，同一个名词就指那个结果，因此它常带所有格。

senses.title: A ruling by a court
senses.definition: the formal decision of a court that settles the rights of the parties
senses.definitionCN: 法院了结各方权利义务的正式决定
senses.example: The judgment ordered the company to restore the wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 判决责令该公司恢复这片湿地。
senses.why: Law was the earliest home of the word, and the courtroom sense never faded even as the everyday sense broadened.
senses.whyCN: 法律是这个词最早的家，即便日常义后来拓宽，法庭义也从未消退。

senses.title: A formal decision of a tribunal
senses.definition: an award or finding issued by a panel, arbitrator or competition jury
senses.definitionCN: 由评审团、仲裁人或竞赛评委作出的裁定或评定
senses.example: The arbitration judgment awarded costs to the smaller firm.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁裁决把费用判给了那家较小的公司。
senses.why: Any body that must settle a dispute borrows the courtroom noun, so the sense travels from courts to arbitrators and juries.
senses.whyCN: 任何必须了结争议的机构都会借用这个法庭名词，于是这一义从法院延伸到仲裁人与评委。

senses.title: The exercise of judicial authority
senses.definition: the act of deciding as one lawfully entitled to decide, as in the phrase to sit in judgment
senses.definitionCN: 以合法资格作出裁断的行为，如「坐在审判席上」这一说法
senses.example: The commission sits in judgment on complaints about broadcasters.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会对针对广播机构的投诉行使裁断权。
senses.why: The noun can name not just the ruling but the authority being exercised, which is why it survives in formal legal phrasing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词不只指裁决，也指被行使的权威，因此它在正式法律措辞中留存。

senses.title: Divine judgment
senses.definition: in religious language, the verdict of a higher power on human conduct
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语言中，更高力量对人类行为的裁决
senses.example: The sermon warned of judgment and of mercy in the same breath.
senses.exampleCN: 布道在同一口气里既警告审判，也提到怜悯。
senses.why: Religious language took the courtroom image and moved the judge upward, so the word acquired a sense no human court can supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言借走法庭意象，把审判者移到天上，这个词于是获得人间法庭给不了的义项。

senses.title: Critical evaluation in a field
senses.definition: the trained assessment of quality in a craft, as in editorial or artistic judgment
senses.definitionCN: 对某一行业或艺术品质的专业评估
senses.example: The curator's judgment on the drawings was trusted by three museums.
senses.exampleCN: 这位策展人对这批素描的品评得到三家博物馆信赖。
senses.why: Where a field has standards but no rules, practitioners rely on trained judgment, and the word names that reliance.
senses.whyCN: 当一个领域有标准却无规则时，从业者依赖训练出的判断，这个词就指这种依赖。

senses.title: A judgment call
senses.definition: a decision that must rest on opinion because the rules and data leave the case open
senses.definitionCN: 规则与数据都未定论、只能凭看法作出的决定
senses.example: Whether to publish before the holiday was a judgment call.
senses.exampleCN: 要不要在假期前发表，是个只能凭判断的决定。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks the point where calculation stops and opinion must act, which is the everyday survival of the old authority sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定说法标出计算终止、看法必须上场的那一刻，也是古老权威义在日常中的遗留。

intro.en: Judgment comes through Old French from Latin judicium, built on judex 'judge', which joins jus 'law, right' to dicere 'to say, declare'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: judgment 经古法语来自拉丁语 judicium，其基础是 judex「法官」，由 jus「法律、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Jus meant 'law, right, justice'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to the verb for swearing an oath is a hypothesis.
items.cn: jus 意为「法律、权利、正义」。其更早来源未得到证明；有人提出它与表「发誓」的动词有关，那只是假说。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. The same verb builds dictate, predict and verdict.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、宣告」。同一个动词还构成 dictate、predict 与 verdict。

items.en: Jus plus dicere produced judex 'one who declares the law', hence the judge.
items.cn: jus 加 dicere 构成 judex「宣告法律的人」，即法官。

items.en: The noun judicium named the declaring of a right, then the ruling itself and the faculty of ruling well.
items.cn: 名词 judicium 既指宣告权利，也指裁决本身，以及善于裁断的能力。

items.en: Old French jugement carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, where legal use came first and general use followed.
items.cn: 古法语 jugement 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，法律用法先行，一般用法随后。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is recorded only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of jus is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语用例只有约略记载；jus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are routinely mixed up with judgment; group two holds near neighbours for an opinion or a ruling.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，常与本词张冠李戴；第二组是表示看法或裁定的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the official and the verb for what that official does; judgment is the ruling or the capacity, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 作名词指法官，作动词指法官所做的事；judgment 指裁决或能力，不指人。

entries.definition: An adjective for the court system and its procedures, not for a person's opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容法院系统及其程序，而非个人的看法。

entries.definition: Built to mean full of good judgment, so it is a compliment; it is not the adjective of judgmental.
entries.definitionCN: 构成上意为「富于良好判断」，因此是褒义；它并不是 judgmental 的形容词原形。

entries.definition: Built with the prefix meaning 'before' plus the same judging root, so it literally means a judgment formed in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「在前」的前缀加同一个「判断」词根构成，字面就是「事先形成的判断」。

entries.definition: The formal finding of a jury, literally a true saying; it is the courtroom sense of judgment made specific.
entries.definitionCN: 指陪审团的正式认定，字面是「如实说出」，是法院义的具体化。

entries.definition: A view held without the weight of authority; judgment suggests that the view was earned by weighing.
entries.definitionCN: 指所持的看法，不带权威分量；judgment 暗示这看法是权衡得来的。

entries.definition: The process or result of measuring something against criteria; judgment adds the personal act of deciding.
entries.definitionCN: 指按标准衡量的过程或结果；judgment 多了「人作出裁断」这一层。

entries.definition: The ability to see subtle differences, especially in quality; judgment stresses the conclusion rather than the seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 指看出细微差别的能力，尤其在品质上；judgment 强调结论而非看见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、真实的词族与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: The Latin noun joins law and declaring, so judgment is law spoken out loud.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁名词把「法律」与「宣告」连在一起，因此判断就是被说出来的法。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judicial, judicious, judiciary, prejudice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judicial、judicious、judiciary、prejudice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the courtroom origin: pass judgment, sit in judgment, a court judgment.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出法庭出身：作出评判、坐在审判席上、法院判决。

normal.en: The everyday phrase a judgment call marks the point where rules run out.
normal.cn: 日常说法「凭判断的决定」标出规则用尽的那一刻。

normal.en: British writing often spells the noun judgement, while American writing prefers judgment.
normal.cn: 英式写作常拼作 judgement，美式写作多用 judgment。

abstract.en: Picture a balance whose pointer stops only after the weights are all placed.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，砝码全部放好之后指针才停住。

abstract.en: Picture a gavel that falls once and ends every argument in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一把法槌落下一次，房间里所有争论就此结束。

abstract.en: Picture a critic who looks at a painting for a long time before saying a single word.
abstract.cn: 想象一位评论家看画很久，才说出一句话。

examples.en: The recruiter trusted her judgment more than the test scores.
examples.cn: 招聘者更信她的判断，而不是那些测验分数。

examples.en: The court issued a judgment that reopened the old case.
examples.cn: 法院作出判决，让这桩旧案重新开庭。

examples.en: Whether to speak now or wait was a judgment call.
examples.cn: 现在开口还是再等等，是个只能凭判断的决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「judge 法官 + ment 行为」——法官作出的，就是判决与判断

root: 拉丁 judicium「裁断」= judex「法官」+ 名词后缀；judex 又由 jus「法律、权利」与 dicere「说、宣告」构成；jus 更深来源不确定。英语 judgment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of declaring what is right: a capacity, an opinion, a court's ruling, an arbitrator's award, the authority behind it, a heavenly verdict, a craft's evaluation and a call made where rules stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：宣告何为正当。它依次是能力、看法、法院判决、仲裁裁定、背后的权威、天上的裁决、行业内的品评，以及规则用尽处凭看法作出的决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance whose pointer trembles and then stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上的指针抖了一下，然后停住。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND PRODUCT: the ability to weigh and the opinion it produces are the same act seen inside and outside.
branches.cn: 能力与产物：权衡的能力与它产出的看法，是同一动作的内外两面。

branches.en: COURT AND AUTHORITY: a ruling and the lawful power to issue it are inseparable in legal use.
branches.cn: 判决与权威：在法律用法里，裁决与作出裁决的合法权力不可分。

branches.en: BORROWED COURTROOM: arbitrators and juries use the noun because they too must end a dispute.
branches.cn: 借来的法庭：仲裁人与评委也用这个名词，因为他们同样必须了结争议。

branches.en: UPWARD VERDICT: religion moves the judge above the room, adding a sense no human court supplies.
branches.cn: 向上的裁决：宗教把审判者移到房间之上，增添了人间法庭给不了的义项。

branches.en: TRAINED AND OPEN CASES: professional evaluation and the judgment call both act where written rules fall silent.
branches.cn: 专业与开放情形：行业品评与凭判断的决定，都在明文规则沉默处发挥作用。

intro.en: Judgment is two Latin pieces plus a Latin noun suffix, and the pieces also build the rest of the legal family.
intro.cn: judgment 由两个拉丁成分加一个拉丁名词后缀构成，这些成分还构成整个法律词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin jus gives justice, jurist and jury; Latin dicere gives dictate, predict, verdict and the same ending in prejudice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 jus 衍生 justice、jurist 与 jury；拉丁 dicere 衍生 dictate、predict、verdict，以及 prejudice 中的同一成分。

items.example: The root supplies the legal half of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词义中「法」的那一半。

items.example: The root supplies the speaking that makes a ruling official.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供使裁决成为正式的那种言说。

items.example: The compound produced the name of the official.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词造出了官员的名称。

items.example: The noun is the base that French and English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是法语与英语借用的基础。

items.example: The suffix marks the ruling as something produced and recorded.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把裁决标为被产出、被记录之物。

items.meaning: a ruling or a formed opinion
items.example: English keeps one noun for the act, the result and the capacity.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一个名词指行为、结果与能力。

items.example: The person noun survives beside the abstract one.
items.exampleCN: 指人的名词与抽象名词并存。

items.example: The adjective stays inside the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词留在法律义之内。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun of office into an adjective of system.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把职务名词变成制度形容词。

definition_zh: 呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力；有吸引力
definition_en: an urgent request for help or support; a formal request to a higher court; the quality of being attractive; also to make such a request or to attract
core_image: 把话抛向远处的人，请求他们回应
scene: 洪水过后的村公所里，干部把一张写满名字的纸举起来。 The mayor made an appeal to every household for blankets and clean water.
sceneCN: 这里 appeal 是「呼吁；恳求」（第 1 个义项：向众人提出紧急请求）；句意为「镇长向每一户人家呼吁捐出毛毯和干净的水」。画面里有洪水过后的村公所、写满名字的纸和举着纸的干部。

pos.zh: 名词：呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力
动词：呼吁；恳求；上诉；有吸引力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「有吸引力的；动人的」
由本词加 -ant 构成，义为「上诉人」
由否定前缀 un- 加 appealing 构成，义为「没有吸引力的」

senses.title: An urgent request for help
senses.definition: a serious and often public request for help, money, or support
senses.definitionCN: 严肃而常是公开的请求，求取帮助、钱款或支持
senses.example: The mayor made an appeal to every household for blankets and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 镇长向每一户人家呼吁捐出毛毯和干净的水。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to call out to someone'; the request is a call thrown across distance, hoping for an answer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向某人喊话」；这个请求就是一声抛过距离的呼唤，盼着有人回应。

senses.title: A request to a higher court
senses.definition: a formal request asking a higher court to review and change a legal decision
senses.definitionCN: 正式请求更高一级法院复审并改变某项法律裁决
senses.example: The verdict was overturned on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 那项判决在上诉中被推翻了。
senses.why: In law the call goes upward, to a higher authority; the same 'call out' image is now addressed to the court above.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，呼唤的方向朝上，向更高的权威发出；同一个「喊话」意象如今对着上级法院。

senses.title: The power to attract
senses.definition: the quality in something that makes people like it or want to be near it
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中使人喜欢它或愿意靠近它的特质
senses.example: The old market has a strong appeal for young visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老市场对年轻游客有很强的吸引力。
senses.why: The call is now silent and internal: the object calls to people without asking them for anything, and they answer by coming.
senses.whyCN: 这里的呼唤是无声而向内的：对象向人发出召唤，却不向人索要什么，而人用前来作为回答。

senses.title: To be attractive to someone
senses.definition: as a verb, to please or interest someone, so that they are drawn towards it
senses.definitionCN: 作动词时，表示使人喜欢或感兴趣，从而被它吸引过去
senses.example: The simple plan appeals to people who dislike waste.
senses.exampleCN: 这个简单的方案打动了不喜欢浪费的人。
senses.why: Here the attraction is felt as an answer: the plan calls, and the people find themselves responding.
senses.whyCN: 这里的吸引力被感受为一种回应：方案发出召唤，人们发现自己响应了。

senses.title: To call upon reason or feelings
senses.definition: in the phrase appeal to, to invoke something such as reason, emotion, or a principle as support
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 appeal to，表示借助理智、情感或某项原则来作为支撑
senses.example: The speaker appealed to the audience's sense of fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲者诉诸听众的公平感。
senses.why: The oldest layer of 'call out' returns: one does not ask for aid but summons a faculty in the listener and asks it to decide.
senses.whyCN: 「喊话」最古老的一层回来了：不是求取援助，而是召唤听者内心的一种能力，请它来作判断。

intro.en: Appeal goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to call out to someone', and every later sense is a variation on that call.
intro.cn: appeal 可上溯到一个表示「向某人喊话」的拉丁动词，此后每个义项都是那声呼唤的变奏。

items.en: Appellare meant 'to address, call upon', built from ad- 'to' and pellere 'drive'; the sense is of driving words towards someone.
items.cn: appellare 表示「向……说话、召唤」，由 ad-「向」与 pellere「驱动」构成；意象是把话推向某人。

items.en: The verb passes into Old French as apeler, 'to call, to summon', and English borrows it.
items.cn: 这个动词进入古法语作 apeler，义为「呼叫、传唤」，英语随后借入。

items.en: English appeal first appears in law, meaning to call a case up to a higher court.
items.cn: 英语 appeal 最早出现在法律语境，意为把案件上诉到更高一级法院。

items.en: The general sense 'urgent request' develops, and the noun can name a plea for help or money.
items.cn: 一般义「紧急请求」发展出来，名词可指为帮助或钱款发出的恳求。

items.en: The sense of attractiveness appears: a thing can appeal to people without asking them for anything.
items.cn: 吸引力义出现：事物可以不向人索求什么，却仍对人发出召唤。

items.en: The word works in law, charity, advertising and argument, always keeping the shape of a call directed at someone.
items.cn: 这个词活跃于法律、慈善、广告与论辩之中，始终保留着「向某人发出呼唤」的形状。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same 'call out' verb; the near-meaning group gathers requests, legal challenges and forms of attraction.
note.cn: 形近组收同出那个「喊话」动词的词；近义组收请求、法律申诉与吸引力方面的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning attractive or touching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有吸引力的；动人的」，由本词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A noun for the person who brings an appeal in a legal case.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上诉人」，指在法律案件中提出上诉的一方。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a name or title, from the same 'call' verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「名称、称号」，同出表示「呼叫」的那个动词。

entries.definition: To ask urgently and emotionally for something.
entries.definitionCN: 急切而带感情地请求，语气比 appeal 更卑微。

entries.definition: To ask for something politely, without the urgency of appeal.
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌地提出请求，没有 appeal 那种紧急与公开性。

entries.definition: A formal written request signed by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多人签名的正式书面请求，与 appeal 的公开呼吁义接近。

entries.definition: The quality of drawing people towards something.
entries.definitionCN: 把人吸引到某物那里的特质，对应 appeal 的「吸引力」义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'call out' verb and the frames the word takes as noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「喊话」动词，以及这个词作名词与动词时的句式。

normal.en: The core is a call thrown towards someone: ad- 'to' plus pellere 'drive'.
normal.cn: 核心是一声抛向某人的呼唤：ad-「向」加 pellere「驱动」。

normal.en: The legal sense calls upward: a case is appealed to a higher court.
normal.cn: 法律义朝上呼唤：案件被上诉到更高一级法院。

normal.en: The charity sense calls outward: an appeal for blankets and water.
normal.cn: 慈善义朝外呼唤：为毛毯和净水发出呼吁。

normal.en: The attraction sense calls silently: the old market appeals to visitors.
normal.cn: 吸引力义无声地呼唤：老市场吸引着游客。

normal.en: The argument sense summons a faculty: appeal to reason, not to fear.
normal.cn: 论辩义召唤一种能力：诉诸理智，而不是恐惧。

abstract.en: Picture a voice carried across a valley, waiting for someone on the far side to answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一声呼喊越过山谷，等着对面有人回应。

abstract.en: The word is a thread thrown out into the air; the answer may be help, a verdict, or simply a visit.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一根抛向空中的线；回应可能是援助、判决，也可能只是一次到访。

abstract.en: When nobody is asked for anything, the same thread becomes charm: the call that expects no reply.
abstract.cn: 当它不向任何人索求时，同一根线就变成了魅力：一声不期待回应的呼唤。

examples.en: The charity launched an appeal for winter coats.
examples.cn: 那家慈善机构发起了一场募集冬衣的呼吁。

examples.en: The verdict was overturned on appeal.
examples.cn: 那项判决在上诉中被推翻了。

examples.en: The old market has a strong appeal for young visitors.
examples.cn: 这座老市场对年轻游客有很强的吸引力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额皮尔」——镇长举着名单喊「皮尔，你家有毛毯吗」：呼吁

root: appeal 经古法语 apeler 来自拉丁语 appellare「向……说话、召唤」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 pellere「驱动」构成，意象是把话推向某人。十四世纪英语先用于法律，指把案件上诉到更高法院；十六世纪发展出一般义「紧急请求」；十九世纪出现「吸引力」义；现代这个词活跃于法律、慈善、广告与论辩，始终保留「向某人发出呼唤」的形状。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses fan out from one call: an urgent public request, a legal call to a higher court, the silent pull of an attractive thing, the verb of attracting, and the summons of reason or feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从同一声呼唤展开：公开的紧急请求、向更高法院发出的法律呼唤、有魅力之物的无声牵引、表示吸引的动词，以及对理智或情感的召唤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice thrown across a distance, waiting for an answer from the far side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声越过距离的呼唤，等着对面给出回应。

branches.en: THE HELP LINE: the call asks for blankets, money or support.
branches.cn: 求助线：呼唤求取毛毯、钱款或支持。

branches.en: THE LEGAL LINE: the call goes upward to a higher court.
branches.cn: 法律线：呼唤朝上，传给更高一级法院。

branches.en: THE CHARM LINE: the object calls without asking for anything.
branches.cn: 魅力线：对象发出呼唤，却不索要任何东西。

branches.en: THE PULL LINE: people answer the silent call by coming nearer.
branches.cn: 牵引线：人们用靠近来回应那声无声的呼唤。

branches.en: THE SUMMONS LINE: reason or feeling is called upon to decide.
branches.cn: 召唤线：请理智或情感出面作判断。

intro.en: Appeal is a Latin borrowing whose stem is 'call out'; its English derivatives add ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: appeal 是拉丁语借词，词干意为「喊话」；它的英语派生词只是加上常见后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is direct: appellare is the verb behind appeal, and pellere 'drive' sits inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语血统是直接的：appellare 是 appeal 背后的动词，而 pellere「驱动」嵌在其中。

items.meaning: to call upon; a call for help
items.example: The appeal reached the whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 那声呼吁传遍了整个山谷。

items.example: The verb drives words towards the listener.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把话推向听者。

items.example: It aims the call at someone.
Pellere supplies the push inside the word.
items.exampleCN: pellere 提供了这个词内部的推力。

items.example: The idea sounds appealing at first.
items.exampleCN: 这个想法乍听很吸引人。

items.meaning: a person who appeals a case
items.example: The appellant asked for a new hearing.
The region has an old appellation.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区有一个古老的名称。
那栋灰楼看上去毫无吸引力。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成名词的后缀
items.example: It turns the calling verb into an act.
items.exampleCN: 它把「呼唤」这个动词变成一种行为。

latinEntries.example: Appellare is the direct source of appeal.
latinEntries.exampleCN: appellare 是 appeal 的直接来源。
pellere 嵌在 appellare 之中。

definition_zh: 继承（物）；遗产；遗传；（文化）传承；继承权
definition_en: property or a right received from someone who has died, or the transmission of traits and traditions from one generation to the next
core_image: 一只旧木匣装着钥匙与地契，从一双手递到另一双手，匣盖上的封蜡已经裂开
scene: 老宅的钥匙和地契被装进同一个木匣，交到下一代手里。 The eldest daughter received the farm as her inheritance.
sceneCN: 这里 inheritance 指「从去世的亲人那里接下的财产」（第 1 个义项：继承所得的财物）；句意为长女把这座农场作为遗产接了下来。可辨识物件：木匣、黄铜钥匙、地契、裂开的封蜡。

forms.label: 复数（可用，但常作不可数）

senses.title: Property received after a death
senses.titleCN: 从逝者那里接下的财产
senses.definition: money or property passed to an heir after someone dies
senses.definitionCN: 某人去世后传给继承人的钱财或财产
senses.example: She used her inheritance to buy the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 她用继承来的钱买下了那间作坊。
senses.why: The word names what is handed over at death, so the first sense is the concrete estate rather than the act of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指在死亡时被交出的东西，因此第一个义项是具体的遗产，而不是领取的动作。

senses.title: The act or right of inheriting
senses.definition: the legal act or right by which an heir receives an estate
senses.definitionCN: 继承人取得遗产的法定行为或权利
senses.example: The inheritance of the land was disputed for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地的继承权争了多年。
senses.why: Because the noun covers both the thing and the legal relation, English can speak of an inheritance and of the right of inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词同时涵盖财物与法律关系，英语既能说「一份遗产」，也能说「继承权」。
