senses.title: Genetic transmission
senses.definition: the passing of traits from parents to offspring through genes
senses.definitionCN: 性状经基因由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Eye colour shows a simple pattern of inheritance.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛颜色呈现出简单的遗传模式。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century biology borrowed the legal word because traits seemed to be handed down like property.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的生物学借用了这个法律词，因为性状看起来像财产一样被传下去。

senses.title: Cultural heritage
senses.definition: the traditions, language or art received from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 从更早世代接下的传统、语言或艺术
senses.example: The city claims the inheritance of three empires.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市自称承袭了三个帝国的遗产。
senses.why: The legal frame widened to anything received from the past, so a city can inherit an empire's habits of building.
senses.whyCN: 法律框架被拓宽到任何从过去接下的东西，因此一座城市可以继承一个帝国的建造习惯。

senses.title: A burden or condition passed on
senses.titleCN: 一并接下的负担或状况
senses.definition: a debt, problem or condition that comes with what is received
senses.definitionCN: 随所得之物一起到来的债务、问题或状况
senses.example: He carries an inheritance of debt from the previous owner.
senses.exampleCN: 他背上了前任业主留下的一身债务。
senses.why: What is inherited is not always a gift; the word can name the liabilities that arrive with the property.
senses.whyCN: 被继承的不总是礼物；这个词也能指随财产一起到来的负担。

senses.title: Class inheritance in computing
senses.definition: the mechanism by which one class or module takes properties from a parent
senses.definitionCN: 一个类或模块从父级取得属性的机制
senses.example: Class inheritance lets one module reuse another's methods.
senses.exampleCN: 类继承让一个模块可以复用另一个模块的方法。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the family metaphor: a child class receives behaviour from its parent, just as an heir receives property.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用了家庭隐喻：子类从父类取得行为，正如继承人取得财产。

senses.title: Inheritance tax and legal thresholds
senses.definition: the tax charged on an estate before or after it passes to heirs
senses.definitionCN: 遗产传给继承人之前或之后所征的税
senses.example: Inheritance tax applies above a fixed threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产税适用于超过固定起征点的部分。
senses.why: Once the state began taxing transfers at death, the noun became fixed in the compound inheritance tax.
senses.whyCN: 当国家开始对死亡时的财产转移征税后，这个名词就固定于遗产税这一复合词中。

senses.title: A legacy of consequences
senses.definition: the lasting effects that one period or action leaves to those who follow
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期或行动留给后来者的持久影响
senses.example: The reform left an inheritance of distrust.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革留下了一份不信任的遗产。
senses.why: The metaphor treats consequences as an estate: later people receive them whether they want them or not.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把后果当作一份产业：后来者不管愿不愿意都得接收。

intro.en: Inheritance comes from Anglo-French enheritance, from enheriter 'to make an heir', from Late Latin inhereditare, built on heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: inheritance 来自盎格鲁-法语 enheritance，源自动词 enheriter「立为继承人」，再上溯为晚期拉丁 inhereditare，其词干是 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; suggestions linking it to other Indo-European words are hypotheses, and any PIE form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；把它与其他印欧语词联系起来的说法只是假说，凡为其给出的原始印欧语形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Hereditas 'inheritance, heirship' and hereditarius 'of an heir' were formed on the hered- stem.
items.cn: hereditas「继承、继承权」与 hereditarius「继承人的」都建立在 hered- 词干上。

items.en: In- 'in, into' plus hereditare 'to inherit' gave inhereditare 'to appoint as heir'.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 hereditare「继承」构成 inhereditare「立为继承人」。

items.en: Enheriter and its noun enheritance reached English in the fourteenth century; legal use came first, and the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: enheriter 及其名词 enheritance 在 14 世纪进入英语；法律用法最先出现，确切的最早书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word was extended to the transmission of traits, alongside the new science of heredity.
items.cn: 19 世纪，随着遗传学兴起，这个词被扩展到性状传递。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): first dates for the biological sense are approximate, and the pre-Latin origin of heres remains uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：生物学义项的首见年代只是约数，heres 在拉丁语之前的来源仍不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same hered- stem or that merely look similar; group two holds the legal and everyday words for what is left to heirs.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hered- 词干或仅形近的词；第二组是法律与日常语境中表示「留给继承人的东西」的近义词。

entries.tag: same root what is handed down
entries.definition: The same Latin hered- stem, but heritage usually names cultural or family possessions rather than a legal share.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁 hered- 词干，但 heritage 通常指文化或家族传承物，而非法定份额。

entries.definition: The biological transmission of traits, not the property received; the two words split in the nineteenth century.
entries.definitionCN: 指性状的生物传递，而非所收财产；两个词在 19 世纪分化。

entries.definition: The person who receives, not the thing received; the suffix -or marks the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指接收的人，而非所收之物；后缀 -or 标记施事者。

entries.definition: From inhaerere 'to stick in', not heres: the state of being inherent or built into something. The resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 inhaerere「黏附于内」，并非 heres：指内在于某物的状态。相似只是偶然。

entries.definition: A specific gift left in a will; inheritance can also mean the whole estate or the right to it.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱中留下的具体馈赠；inheritance 还可指全部遗产或继承权。

entries.definition: Property given by a will, usually personal items; narrower and more legal than inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱赠予的财产，通常为个人物品；比 inheritance 更窄、更法律化。

entries.definition: The total property a person leaves, before it is divided among heirs.
entries.definitionCN: 某人留下的全部财产，在分配给继承人之前。

entries.definition: Money or property given to an institution, often to produce income; it stresses the lasting gift rather than the heir.
entries.definitionCN: 捐给机构的钱或财产，常用来产生收益；强调持续的馈赠而非继承人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'in' + heres 'heir': being put into the heir's place.
normal.cn: in-「进入」+ heres「继承人」：被放进继承人的位置。

normal.en: The family runs inherit, inheritance, inheritor, inheritable, hereditary and heredity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 inherit、inheritance、inheritor、inheritable、hereditary 与 heredity。

normal.en: Legal use came first; the biological use is a nineteenth-century extension.
normal.cn: 法律用法最先出现，生物学用法是 19 世纪的扩展。

normal.en: In computing, inheritance means a subclass takes methods from its parent.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，inheritance 指子类从父类取得方法。

normal.en: Fixed phrase: inheritance tax.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：遗产税。

abstract.en: Picture a house key passed from hand to hand until the first hand is forgotten.
abstract.cn: 想象一把房门钥匙被一双手传一双手，直到最初那双手被遗忘。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card whose stains are inherited along with the recipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食谱卡，油渍和做法一起被继承下来。

abstract.en: Picture a debt that arrives with the furniture and has no invoice.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债务随家具一起到来，却没有账单。

examples.en: The inheritance was divided equally among the four children.
examples.cn: 遗产在四个孩子之间平均分配。

examples.en: Researchers traced the inheritance of the trait across five generations.
examples.cn: 研究者追踪了这一性状在五代人中的遗传。

examples.en: Class inheritance reduced the amount of code the team had to write.
examples.cn: 类继承减少了团队需要编写的代码量。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ herit（继承人）——进入继承人的位置 → 继承（物）；同根的 heritage 是「传承物」。

root: 拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；经古法语 enheritance 进入英语；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: a box passes at death and becomes property, a right, a biological trait, a culture, a burden, a piece of code, a tax and finally a set of consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：一只匣子在死亡时被递出，成为财产、权利、生物性状、文化、负担、代码、税，最后成为一整套后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden box of keys and deeds passing from one hand to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着钥匙与地契的木匣，从一双手递到另一双手。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND RIGHT: the estate itself and the legal power to receive it.
branches.cn: 财产与权利：遗产本身，以及取得它的法定资格。

branches.en: WHAT IS TRANSMITTED: a trait can arrive like property, and so can a debt.
branches.cn: 被传递之物：性状可以像财产一样到来，债务也可以。

branches.en: CULTURE: buildings, language and habits are received from earlier generations.
branches.cn: 文化：建筑、语言与习惯从更早世代接下。

branches.en: COMPUTING: a child class receives behaviour from its parent class.
branches.cn: 计算机：子类从父类取得行为。

branches.en: TAX AND CONSEQUENCE: the state takes a share, and later people receive the effects.
branches.cn: 税与后果：国家取走一份，后来者接收影响。

intro.en: Inheritance is built from a Latin prefix and the hered- stem, and the same pieces form a large legal and biological family.
intro.cn: inheritance 由拉丁前缀与 hered- 词干构成，这些成分组成了一个庞大的法律与生物词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, inherit and inheritance; in- adds the sense of entering a position.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、inherit 与 inheritance；in- 增添「进入某一位置」的意思。

items.example: The prefix places the receiver inside the heir's position.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把接收者放进继承人的位置。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.

items.meaning: to inherit; to leave as an inheritance
items.example: Hereditare turned the heir into an action.
items.exampleCN: hereditare 把「继承人」变成了动作。

items.example: The Late Latin verb added the legal act of naming an heir.
items.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁动词增添了指定继承人的法律动作。

items.structure: English verb from Old French enheriter
items.example: She inherited the house from her aunt.
items.exampleCN: 她从姑妈那里继承了这所房子。

items.meaning: the estate or the act of receiving it
items.example: The inheritance was divided among the children.
items.exampleCN: 遗产在孩子们之间分配。
继承人在契据上签了字。

items.example: The trait is inheritable in a simple pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这一性状以简单模式可遗传。

definition_en: a large area of land with a house, or all the property a person owns
core_image: 一片带大房子的土地，四周是树和围墙
scene: 他祖父留下了一座带花园的老庄园，如今成了当地的景点。 His grandfather left an old estate with a garden, which is now a local attraction.
sceneCN: 这里 estate 是「庄园」（第 1 个义项：带房屋的大片乡间土地）；句意：他祖父留下了一座带花园的老庄园，如今成了当地的景点。

senses.title: A large country property
senses.definition: a large area of land in the country with one main house
senses.definitionCN: 乡间带有主屋的大片土地
senses.example: The family has lived on the estate for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家族已在庄园里住了好几代。
senses.why: The Latin source means state or condition, and land held in one state became an estate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为状态，处于同一状态的土地就成为一个庄园。

senses.title: Property and land
senses.definition: land or buildings owned by someone
senses.definitionCN: 某人拥有的土地或建筑
senses.example: He works in real estate in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城里做房地产生意。
senses.why: Property is the modern everyday sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 财产是这个词在现代的日常义项。

senses.title: Property left at death
senses.definition: all the money and property a person leaves when they die
senses.definitionCN: 一个人去世时留下的全部钱财与财产
senses.example: Her estate was divided among three children.
senses.exampleCN: 她的遗产分给了三个孩子。
senses.why: What a person owns at the end of life is their whole estate.
senses.whyCN: 一个人生命结束时拥有的全部财产就是其遗产。

intro.en: Estate comes from Old French estat, from Latin status, a state or condition.
intro.cn: estate 源自古法语 estat，源自拉丁语 status（状态、身份）。

items.en: Status means a state or standing.
items.cn: status 意为状态或身份。

items.en: Estat means condition or rank.
items.cn: estat 意为状况或等级。

items.en: Estate names the land and position of a family.
items.cn: estate 指家族的土地与地位。

items.en: Estate covers property and inheritance.
items.cn: estate 涵盖房地产与遗产。

items.en: Real estate names land and buildings.
items.cn: real estate 指土地与建筑。

note.en: Estate is close to property and land, and has a special legal sense.
note.cn: estate 与财产、土地相近，并有专门的法律含义。

entries.definition: more than one estate
entries.definitionCN: 多个庄园

entries.definition: a condition or country
entries.definitionCN: 状态；国家

entries.definition: social position
entries.definitionCN: 地位

entries.definition: things that belong to someone
entries.definitionCN: 财产

entries.definition: the solid surface of the earth
entries.definitionCN: 土地

entries.definition: property passed down after a death
entries.definitionCN: 遗产

normalIntro.en: An estate is a whole state of property gathered under one name.
normalIntro.cn: estate 就是一个名字之下聚拢起来的全部财产状态。

normal.en: A country estate is a large house with land.
normal.cn: a country estate 是带土地的乡间大宅。

normal.en: Real estate means land and buildings.
normal.cn: real estate 意为土地与建筑。

normal.en: An estate agent helps people buy property.
normal.cn: estate agent 帮人买房。

normal.en: A person's estate is all they own at death.
normal.cn: 一个人的 estate 是其去世时的全部财产。

normal.en: Compare property: property is any owned thing, an estate is the whole holding.
normal.cn: 对比 property：property 是任何所有物，estate 是全部产业。

abstract.en: Picture a long drive leading to a stone house.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的车道通向石屋。

abstract.en: Imagine a map with one large piece shaded and named.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有一大块被涂色并标名。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed box holding everything a family owns.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的箱子装着一个家庭的全部所有物。

examples.en: The old estate has a huge garden and a lake.
examples.cn: 这座古老庄园有巨大的花园和一个湖。

examples.en: Prices in real estate have risen sharply.
examples.cn: 房地产价格大幅上涨。

examples.en: The estate was divided equally among the heirs.
examples.cn: 遗产在继承人之间平均分配。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estate」听起来像「一块地」——带房子的整片土地，就是庄园或地产；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 status（状态、身份）→ 古法语 estat → estate，核心义「处于同一名下的整片土地与财产」。

sensesIntro.en: Estate first means a large country property, then land and buildings, and finally everything a person leaves at death.
sensesIntro.cn: estate 先指乡间大庄园，再指土地与建筑，最后指去世时留下的全部遗产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled area of land with one large house at its center.
core.cn: 核心意象：围起来的土地上坐落着一栋大房子。

branches.en: A country property is the traditional sense.
branches.cn: 乡间庄园是传统义项。

branches.en: Land and buildings make up modern property.
branches.cn: 土地与建筑构成现代房地产。

branches.en: The whole holding passes on at death.
branches.cn: 全部产业在去世时被传承。

branches.en: An estate is both a home and a piece of property.
branches.cn: 庄园既是家，也是财产。

branches.en: Property owned at death forms the inheritance.
branches.cn: 去世时拥有的财产构成遗产。

intro.en: Estate comes through Old French estat from Latin status, a state.
intro.cn: estate 经古法语 estat 源自拉丁语 status（状态）。

latinIntro.en: Latin status, a standing or condition, gives state, status and estate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 status（身份、状况）衍生出 state、status 与 estate。

items.example: Old French estat carries the word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 estat 传递了该词。

items.example: Real combines with estate for property.
items.exampleCN: real 与 estate 组合指房地产。

items.example: Real estate is a fixed compound.
Agent combines with estate for a broker.
items.exampleCN: agent 与 estate 组合指经纪人。

items.example: Housing combines with estate for a residential area.
items.exampleCN: housing 与 estate 组合指住宅区。

items.example: A housing estate holds many homes.
items.exampleCN: housing estate 包含许多住宅。

definition_zh: 破产（无力清偿债务的法律状态或司法程序）
definition_en: the legal state or procedure of being unable to pay one's debts
core_image: 一张被砸断的长凳，木片散落在钱币兑换商的门前
scene: 订单断了三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。 After three months without orders, the factory filed for bankruptcy, and its creditors began to register their claims.
sceneCN: 这里指「因无力偿债而进入的法律程序」（第 1 个义项：经法院处理的破产状态）；句意为断单三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。可辨识物件：断凳、法院门牌、债权登记表、封条。

pos.zh: 破产（可数或不可数；复数 bankruptcies）

derivatives.zh: 长凳词根加「断」的分词词根 → 破产的；使破产；破产者
短语意象中的基础名词，义为「长凳、钱桌」→ 银行
否定前缀加「偿付能力」名词 → 无力偿付
基础形容词加动词后缀 → 清算
「断」的词根加名词后缀 → 断裂；破裂

senses.title: The legal status of being unable to pay
senses.titleCN: 无力清偿债务的法律状态
senses.definition: the formal condition, recognised by a court, in which a debtor cannot meet its debts
senses.definitionCN: 经法院认定、债务人无法履行债务的正式状态
senses.example: The court placed the firm in bankruptcy after the payment deadline passed.
senses.exampleCN: 付款期限过后，法院使这家企业进入破产状态。
senses.why: the word began as a broken bench, so the legal status keeps the image of a trader put out of business.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指被砸断的长凳，法律状态因此保留商人被逐出营业的意象。

senses.title: Liquidation of the debtor's assets
senses.titleCN: 变卖债务人资产以清偿
senses.definition: the procedure in which assets are sold and the proceeds divided among creditors
senses.definitionCN: 变卖资产并把所得分给债权人的程序
senses.example: Bankruptcy ended with the mill sold and the workers paid first.
senses.exampleCN: 破产以工厂被出售、工人先获清偿而结束。
senses.why: if the business cannot continue, the assets must be turned into money so creditors can be paid in order.
senses.whyCN: 企业若无法继续，资产必须换成钱，债权人才能按顺序获偿。

senses.title: Reorganisation instead of sale
senses.definition: a procedure that keeps the business running while debts are restructured
senses.definitionCN: 在重组债务的同时让企业继续运营的程序
senses.example: The airline used bankruptcy to renegotiate its leases, not to close.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司借破产重新谈租约，而非关门。
senses.why: a business may be worth more alive than sold, so the law offers a route that keeps it running while debts are rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 企业活着可能比卖掉更值钱，法律因此提供一条让它继续运营、同时重组债务的路径。

senses.title: Personal bankruptcy
senses.definition: the same legal route taken by an individual rather than a company
senses.definitionCN: 由个人而非企业走上的同一法律路径
senses.example: Personal bankruptcy cleared the medical debts but ruined her credit.
senses.exampleCN: 个人破产免除了医疗债务，却毁了她的信用。
senses.why: a person can owe more than he owns just as a company can, so the same procedure is offered to individuals.
senses.whyCN: 个人也会像企业一样欠得比拥有的多，同一程序因此也向个人开放。

senses.title: The figurative collapse of an idea or system
senses.titleCN: 观念或体系的比喻性崩解
senses.definition: a total failure of a scheme, theory or institution, without any court involved
senses.definitionCN: 计划、理论或机构的彻底失败，与法院无关
senses.example: The report described the plan as a moral and economic bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称该计划在道义与经济上均已破产。
senses.why: the broken bench can be imagined anywhere, so any total failure is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 断凳可以被想象在任何地方，任何彻底的失败便都用同一个词描述。

senses.title: Moral bankruptcy in public life
senses.titleCN: 公共生活中的道德破产
senses.definition: the loss of credibility or ethical standing of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体失去公信力或道德地位
senses.example: The scandal exposed the moral bankruptcy of the leadership.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻暴露出领导层的道德破产。
senses.why: when credibility rather than money is gone, the word still fits, because nothing is left to pay with.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的是公信力而非金钱时，这个词仍然合用，因为已无东西可付。

senses.title: The act of filing a petition
senses.definition: the formal step by which a debtor or creditor starts the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 债务人或债权人启动程序的形式步骤
senses.example: The filing for bankruptcy came on a Friday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 破产申请是在一个周五下午提交的。
senses.why: the procedure begins with a document, so the act of filing is spoken of as the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 程序从一份文书开始，因此提交的动作本身被当作事件来说。

senses.title: Bankruptcy protection and the automatic stay
senses.definition: the court order that pauses collection and lawsuits while the case proceeds
senses.definitionCN: 案件进行期间暂停追债与诉讼的法院命令
senses.example: Bankruptcy protection stopped the bank from seizing the equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 破产保护阻止了银行扣押设备。
senses.why: creditors would otherwise race to seize assets, so a court order freezes collection while the case is sorted out.
senses.whyCN: 否则债权人会抢先扣押资产，法院命令因此在案件理清期间冻结追债。

senses.title: Fraudulent bankruptcy
senses.definition: the offence of hiding or transferring assets before or during insolvency
senses.definitionCN: 在无力偿付之前或期间藏匿、转移资产的罪行
senses.example: Two directors were charged with fraudulent bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 两名董事被控欺诈性破产。
senses.why: hiding assets before the case defeats the purpose of the law, so the conduct is made a separate offence.
senses.whyCN: 在案发前藏匿资产会摧毁法律的目的，因此该行为被单列为罪行。

intro.en: Bankruptcy comes from Italian banca rotta 'broken bench', the table of a money changer who could not pay. The image reached English through French and Latin forms in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bankruptcy 来自意大利语 banca rotta「被砸断的长凳」，即无力清偿的钱币兑换商的桌子。这一意象于 16 世纪经法语与拉丁形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: A banca was the bench or table where a money changer and his coins sat in a public square.
items.cn: banca 指钱币兑换商与他的钱币在公共广场上占据的长凳或桌子。

items.en: Rumpere meant 'to break', and its participle ruptus supplied the second half of banca rotta.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「打断」，其分词 ruptus 提供 banca rotta 的后一半。

items.en: In Italian practice a trader who could not pay might have his bench broken, a public sign that he could no longer do business.
items.cn: 在意大利的惯例中，无力清偿的商人可能被砸断长凳，公开表明他不能再做生意。

items.en: French borrowed the image as banqueroute, and English took the noun in the sixteenth century in forms such as bankrupt.
items.cn: 法语把这个意象借为 banqueroute，英语于 16 世纪以 bankrupt 一类形式吸收该名词。

items.en: The abstract noun bankruptcy was formed in English on the model of French, adding the ending that names a state or procedure.
items.cn: 抽象名词 bankruptcy 在英语中仿法语构成，加上表示状态或程序的词尾。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries turned the image into a statute-based procedure with liquidation, reorganisation, protection and criminal forms.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪把这一意象变成以成文法为基础的程序，包含清算、重整、保护与犯罪形态。

note.en: Group one holds words from the broken-bench image or from breaking; group two holds legal and financial terms that are often used as if they were synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是出自「断凳」意象或「打断」词根的词；第二组是常被当作同义词使用的法律与金融术语。

entries.definition: A debtor legally declared unable to pay, or the act of making someone so; bankruptcy is the state or case.
entries.definitionCN: 指被依法宣告无力清偿的债务人，或使某人如此的行为；bankruptcy 指状态或案件。

entries.definition: The institution that grew from the money changer's bench; the shared origin is invisible in modern use.
entries.definitionCN: 指由钱币商长凳发展而来的机构；共同的来源在现代用法中已看不出来。

entries.definition: A break or burst, often of a pipe or a relationship; it has nothing to do with money.
entries.definitionCN: 指断裂或爆裂，常用于管道或关系；与金钱无关。

entries.definition: To break into something in progress; the prefix means between, and no debt is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指打断进行中的事情；前缀意为「在……之间」，不涉债务。

entries.definition: The accounting state of owing more than one owns; bankruptcy is the legal procedure that may follow.
entries.definitionCN: 指欠得比拥有的多的会计状态；bankruptcy 是随后可能启动的法律程序。

entries.definition: The selling off of assets; it is one form bankruptcy can take, not the whole procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指变卖资产；它是破产可能采取的一种形式，而非整个程序。

entries.definition: Failure to pay on a due date; a default can occur without any bankruptcy case being opened.
entries.definitionCN: 指到期未付；违约可以在未启动任何破产案件时发生。

entries.definition: Control of a company given to an outside officer for creditors; it is a separate legal route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把公司控制权交给外部官员以维护债权人；是另一条法律路径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real pieces of the compound, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The picture is a broken bench: a money changer's table smashed so he cannot trade.
normal.cn: 图景是一张断凳：钱币兑换商的桌子被砸，无法再做买卖。

normal.en: The family runs bankrupt, bankruptcy, bank, rupture, interrupt, disrupt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括破产的、破产、银行、断裂、打断、扰乱。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the steps: file for, declare, protection, proceedings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出步骤：申请、宣布、保护、程序。

normal.en: The bench survives in bank, and the breaking survives in rupture.
normal.cn: 那张长凳留在银行一词里，打断的动作留在断裂一词里。

normal.en: A filing is not a closure: protection can keep the business alive while debts are rebuilt.
normal.cn: 申请并不等于关门：保护可以让企业在债务重组期间继续运营。

abstract.en: Picture splinters of a wooden bench on the stones of a market square.
abstract.cn: 想象木凳的碎片散落在集市广场的石板上。

abstract.en: Picture a shop with the shutters down but the lights still on inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店拉下卷帘，里面的灯却还亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a promise collapsing under its own weight, with no court in sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺在自身重量下崩塌，四周并无法院。

examples.en: The chain filed for bankruptcy after the rent review doubled its costs.
examples.cn: 租金复核使成本翻倍后，这家连锁店申请破产。

examples.en: Bankruptcy protection gave the airline time to renegotiate its leases.
examples.cn: 破产保护给了这家航空公司重新谈租约的时间。

examples.en: Analysts spoke of the bankruptcy of the theory, not of any company.
examples.cn: 分析师说的是这一理论的破产，而非任何公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「长凳」与「断」两个词根加名词后缀——钱币商的长凳被砸断，做不成买卖 → 破产

root: 意大利语 banca rotta「断凳」：banca「长凳、钱桌」加 rotta，后者出自拉丁 ruptus／rumpere「打断」。经法语 banqueroute 于 16 世纪进入英语，抽象名词仿法语构成。同根词有 rupture、interrupt、disrupt、corrupt、abrupt。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one case: the legal status, the sale of assets, the attempt to keep trading, the individual route, the collapse of an idea, moral collapse, the filing itself, the protection that pauses creditors, and the criminal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个案件展开：法律状态、变卖资产、设法继续经营、个人路径、观念的崩解、道德崩解、申请的动作、暂停追债的保护，以及犯罪形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smashed bench on the stones of a market square.
core.cn: 核心意象：集市广场石板上的一张被砸断的长凳。

branches.en: STATUS AND PETITION: the condition is declared, and someone must file to start it.
branches.cn: 状态与申请：条件被宣告，且必须有人提交申请才能启动。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: the assets are sold, or the business is kept alive and the debts rebuilt.
branches.cn: 两种结局：资产被变卖，或企业继续存活、债务被重组。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL: a person can take the same route as a company.
branches.cn: 个人：一个人可以走与企业相同的路径。

branches.en: THE WORD WITHOUT A COURT: an idea or a leadership can be called bankrupt in plain speech.
branches.cn: 无需法院的词：观念或领导层可以在日常语言中被称为破产。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND ABUSE: the law pauses collection, and the law also punishes hidden assets.
branches.cn: 保护与滥用：法律暂停追债，法律也惩罚藏匿资产。

intro.en: Bankruptcy joins the bench of the money changer with a Latin participle for broken; the breaking root also builds rupture, interrupt and corrupt.
intro.cn: bankruptcy 把钱币兑换商的长凳与表示「被打断」的拉丁分词连在一起；这一词根还构成 rupture、interrupt 与 corrupt。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere 'to break' and its participle ruptus supply the second half of the word; banca is Italian for the bench.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rumpere「打断」及其分词 ruptus 提供该词的后一半；banca 是意大利语中的长凳。

items.meaning: the state of a broken bench

items.example: The meeting came to an abrupt end.
